Crucially, beat perception arises even in syncopated musical rhythms, which only weakly cue the beat periodicity. However, syncopated rhythms are often looped in music, suggesting that repetition of rhythmic patterns may facilitate beat perception by providing a periodic structure at a supra-second timescale.

title: Intra-tumoral lymphocyte scoring in colorectal cancer: improving prognostic utility and correlation with underlying cancer biology
creator: Patrick L. Wagner, Jianwu Xie, Devin C. Flaherty, Hyun Park, Chelsea Knotts, Justine Debelius, Curtis Tilves, Neda Dadgar, Kunhong Xiao, Ali H. Zaidi, Louis Gil Acevedo, William LaFramboise, Ni Zhao, Cynthia Sears, Noel Mueller
description: BackgroundIntra-tumoral lymphocytes hold prognostic and predictive significance in colorectal cancer (CRC). The internationally validated Immunoscore™ predicts CRC survival risk by averaging percentile scores of tumor-associated CD3+ and CD8+ cell densities, but is limited by increased cost, intra-tumoral heterogeneity and omission of other immunologic variables of importance.

title: 742. Psychogenic Nonepileptic Seizures Following Graves’ Disease Surgery: A Case Report
creator: A Canli Isler
description: BackgroundPsychogenic nonepileptic seizures (PNES) are functional neurological events that resemble epileptic seizures but occur in the absence of epileptiform activity on electroencephalography (Tilahun and Bautista, 2022). PNES are frequently misdiagnosed as epileptic seizures, particularly in acute and perioperative settings, resulting in unnecessary antiepileptic treatment, repeated neuroimaging, and prolonged hospitalizations (Lehn et al., 2021).

title: Introduction to the Research Results of Coronavirus Disease 2019 Big Data (K-COV-N) and the Corresponding Utilization Plan
creator: Hyeryeon Lee, Suhyeon Choi, Eunjin Eom, Gyeong Hee Song, Seong Sun Kim, 혜련 이, 수현 최, 은진 엄, 경희 송, 성순 김
description: As part of the effort to establish a scientific basis for quarantine policies aimed at responding to new infectious diseases based on the experience of responding to coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (KDCA) and National Health Insurance Service promoted the establishment of health information big data and signed a business agreement (April 29, 2021).

title: Effect of irrigation and bio-fertilizers on morphological and bio-chemical traits of milk thistle
creator: Jafar Ghaffarzadeh, Reza Amirnia, Amir Rahimi, Afshin Khorsand
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The milk thistle plant strengthens the body’s immune system and is one of the top-selling medicinal plants in the world in terms of turnover. Considering the water crisis in Iran and especially in the northwest of Iran, which has led to the drying up of Lake Urmia, the cultivation of crops with low water requirements is considered important under the conditions of water scarcity.

title: 501. 2-year real-world clinical outcomes of vagus nerve stimulation for higher-grade treatment-resistant depression
creator: Y Domany, K Feffer, I Straus, Z Feldman, A Solomon, E Blomhof-Bris, R Nega, G Gal, A Hadar
description: BackgroundMajor depressive disorder (MDD) is a leading cause of disability. Despite multiple treatment strategies, a substantial proportion of patients do not achieve adequate symptom relief. This subgroup is known as treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and poses clinical and challenges. Among them, individuals with higher-grade TRD (HG-TRD)—defined as failure of at least four adequate treatment interventions—have limited treatment options.

title: Genetic determinism of fatty acid composition in liver, muscle, backfat and plasma and its link to immunocompetence and performance in pigs
creator: Carles Hernández-Banqué, Junhui Liu, Teodor Jové-Juncà, Olga González-Rodríguez, Manuel Portero-Otín, Josep Maria Folch, Raquel Quintanilla, Maria Ballester
description: Fatty acids are a diverse group of lipid molecules that play essential roles in energy metabolism, cellular differentiation and signalling mechanisms. The objective of this study was to explore the genetic determinism of fatty acid composition across backfat, liver, muscle and plasma and its association with immunocompetence and performance traits in pigs.

title: 410. Comparative neurophysiological signatures of psychedelics, stimulants and anesthetics in rodent cortical activity
creator: B Richardson, J O'Byrne, V Bruno, S Comai, R Carhart-Harris, G Gobbi
description: BackgroundPsychedelics induce altered states of consciousness (AOC) with profound perceptual, cognitive, and emotional shifts, often linked to positive therapeutic outcomes. Although serotonergic psychedelics such as psilocybin, LSD, and 5-MeO-DMT share receptor targets, they differ in behavioral and neural effects. How these compounds alter cortical dynamics relative to other consciousness-modulating agents, including dopaminergic stimulants and anesthetics, remains unclear.

title: Quality and accuracy of scoliosis-related short videos on TikTok reviewed in China in August 2025
creator: Qinxin Zhou, Jianzeng Shen, Dongdong Cao, Weijie Yu, Jixin Chen
description: Scoliosis is a common spinal disorder that affects 2–4% of adolescents worldwide. With the rise of short-video platforms like TikTok, they have increasingly played a significant role in health information dissemination. However, the quality and accuracy of scoliosis-related video content on these platforms have not been thoroughly studied.

title: 331. Rapid antidepressant effects of inhaled GH001 in treatment-resistant depression: results from a phase 2b, double-blind, randomized controlled trial with 6-month follow-up
creator: W J Cubala, K Doolin, F Ryan, M E Thase, V Valcheva, B T Baune
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTreatment-resistant depression (TRD) represents a particularly challenging form of major depressive disorder (MDD), defined by an inadequate response to at least two antidepressants given at adequate dose and duration within the current depressive episode. TRD affects nearly one-third of individuals with MDD and is consistently linked to greater psychiatric and medical comorbidity, increased rates of hospitalization, elevated suicide risk, and a significantly reduced quality of life compared to non-resistant depression.

title: The fate of manuscripts rejected by the Turkish Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation
creator: Duygu Geler Külcü, Birkan Sonel Tur, Burcu Yanık, Şebnem Koldaş Doğan, Ayşe Nur Bardak, Coşkun Zateri, Deniz Evcik
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objectives The aim of this study was to evaluate the fate of the articles after they were rejected from the Turkish Journal of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (Turk J Phys Med Rehab). Materials and methods Between January 2016 and December 2021, rejected manuscripts by the Turk J Phys Med Rehab were retrospectively analyzed and whether these rejected articles were published in another journal was identified.

title: MRI-based deep learning and radiomics pipeline for myxoid liposarcoma: a feasibility study in a rare sarcoma
creator: Jakob Steiner, Marcus Bloice, Jasminka Igrec, Bernadette Liegl-Atzwanger, Andreas Leithner, Michael Fuchsjäger, Martin Urschler
description: Myxoid liposarcoma (MLPS) is a rare soft tissue sarcoma characterized by histopathological variability, which poses challenges for accurate grading and treatment planning. This study evaluated the feasibility of an automated MRI-based pipeline that combines deep learning and radiomics for non-invasive tumor assessment.

title: 603. The gut microbiome is essential for stress-induced eating behaviour: Implications for obesity and microbiota-targeted interventions
creator: M Tufvesson-Alm, H Schellekens
description: BackgroundObesity is associated with both anxiety and depression, often leading to maladaptive emotional eating behaviours that cause and maintain obesity, such as stress-eating. While the causes behind problematic eating behaviours are poorly understood, it is vital to target these behaviours in order to help patients develop and maintain healthy eating patterns and to treat obesity sustainably.

title: AI-powered SPOT imaging for enhanced myocardial scar detection and quantification
creator: Aurelien Bustin, Matthias Stuber, Victor de Villedon de Naide, Manuel Villegas-Martinez, Kalvin Narceau, Thaïs Génisson, Théo Richard, Pauline Gut, Valery Ozenne, Marion Constantin, Guido Caluori, Konstantinos Vlachos, Géraldine Montier, Daphné Pasche, Théo Bedague, Jean-David Maes, Soumaya Sridi, C
description: Cardiovascular disease is the leading global cause of death, underscoring the need for accurate assessment of myocardial injury. The current gold standard, bright-blood late gadolinium enhanced MRI, suffers from poor contrast at the blood-scar interface, reducing sensitivity for subendocardial scar detection and limiting reproducibility. Moreover, reliance on expert manual analysis makes interpretation labor-intensive and variable.

title: Validez y consistencia interna del instrumento HELP Score para evaluar la severidad de los síntomas de la hiperémesis gravídica
creator: Luz Chavarro-Tello, Eliana Retamoso-Paz, Mileidys Correa-Monterrosa
description: RESUMENObjetivos: Determinar la validez y consistencia interna del instrumento HELP Score diseñado para evaluar la severidad de los síntomas de la hiperémesis gravídica.Materiales y métodos: Estudio de validación de un instrumento de medición ensamblado en un estudio de corte transversal, se incluyeron mujeres con hiperémesis gravídica. Se evaluó la validez de contenido mediante el Coeficiente de Validez de Contenido (CVC).

title: 689. What genetics research has told us about the mechanisms of mood disorders
creator: A Mcintosh
description: BackgroundPrior to the advent of large scale genome wide association studies, substantial investments generally failed to reveal major insights into the genetic architecture of mood disorders. Reasons for this include a lack of methodological and data harmonisation, small study sizes and a lack of replication, collaboration and meta-analysis.

title: Isolation and reactivity of sodium benzyl cations
creator: Suban Kundu, Kiran Raj, Alex P Andrews, Thayalan Rajeshkumar, Laurent Maron, Ajay Venugopal
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Carbanions are an important class of reactive species used as nucleophiles in C-C bond-forming reactions. Such reactive carbanions are generated by deprotonating relatively acidic C-H bonds using strong bases like sodium/potassium hydroxides or amides. Lochmann-Schlosser base, consisting of a mixture of alkyl lithium reagents and heavier alkali metal alkoxides, is widely used for the metalation of organic compounds via the deprotonation of weakly acidic C-H bond.

title: 443. Transcriptomic analysis reveals differential mRNA expression in bipolar disorder
creator: A Squassina, M Manchia, C Chillotti, M Bortolomasi, A Minelli, C Pisanu
description: BackgroundBipolar disorder (BD) is a chronic and debilitating psychiatric illness characterized by recurrent episodes of mania and depression. Despite its high heritability, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Gene expression studies, particularly those focusing on total messenger RNA (mRNA), offer a promising avenue for identifying biomarkers and understanding disease pathophysiology.

title: Spatial study of dengue and its association with livestock farming in Bantul Regency, Yogyakarta Province, Indonesia
creator: Dila Hening Windyaraini, Raden Wisnu Nurcahyo, Sitti Rahmah Umniyati, Prima Widayani, Suwarno Hadisusanto
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and Aim:Dengue fever is a recurring arboviral disease. The presence of livestock and domestic animals potentially increases the risk of dengue fever in an area due to the shared habitats of vectors and humans.

title: Ataxin-2-like promotes translation of nonpolyadenylated reovirus mRNA
creator: Xayathed Somoulay, Gavin S Treadaway, Stefanie Hedayati, Myles E Steed, Nathan E Adam, Monico S Williams, John S L Parker, John L Woolford, Laurie A Silva, Gwen M Taylor, Terence S Dermody
description: Mammalian orthoreovirus (reovirus) nonstructural protein μNS nucleates viral factories (VFs), which are sites of viral genome replication, protein synthesis, and particle assembly. Reovirus mRNAs are not polyadenylated, yet these transcripts are efficiently translated. To identify host factors associated with translation in VFs, we conducted a proteomics screen and identified ataxin-2-like (ATXN2L) as a μNS-interacting protein.

title: 737. The panicolytic-like effect of tramadol is modulated by hypothalamic norepinephrine in rats
creator: T B Kirsten, TR R Mazuco
description: BackgroundPanic disorder has a high prevalence; however, there is no fully integrative experimental model for its study. Existing models are mainly based on the evaluation of escape responses induced by aversive stimuli, and the underlying mechanisms are still not fully understood. One hypothesis involves the activation of serotonergic pathway in specific brain areas.

title: Formation of high-aspect-ratio nanocavity in LiF crystal using a femtosecond X-ray free-electron laser pulse
creator: Sergey S. Makarov, Vasily V. Zhakhovsky, Sergey Yu. Grigoryev, Petr Chuprov, Tatiana A. Pikuz, Nail A. Inogamov, Victor A. Khokhlov, Yuri V. Petrov, Evgeniy A. Perov, Vadim Shepelev, Takehisa Shobu, Aki Tominaga, Ludovic Rapp, Saulius Juodkazis, Mikako Makita, Motoaki Nakatsutsumi, Thomas R. Preston
description: Recent research and development into the formation of nanoscale channels as a central component of nanofluidic biochip systems revolutionized the biological and chemical fields. Exploration of new pathways to form nanochannels is increasingly necessary to provide a new generation of analytical tools with accurate control of liquid fluid flow, high selectivity and increased mass flow rate.

title: Exploring the therapeutic potential of Quercus ilex acorn extract in papillomavirus-induced lesions
creator: Beatriz Medeiros-Fonseca, Ana I Faustino-Rocha, Maria João Pires, Maria João Neuparth, Helena Vala, Cármen Vasconcelos-Nóbrega, Irene Gouvinhas, Ana Novo Barros, Maria Inês Dias, Lillian Barros, Margarida M S M Bastos, Lio Gonçalves, Luís Félix, Carlos Venâncio, Rui Medeiros, Rui Miguel Gil da Costa
description: Background and Aim:Papillomaviruses (PVs) infections have been documented in numerous animal species across different regions worldwide. They often exert significant impacts on animal health and livestock production. Scientists have studied natural products for over half a century due to their diverse chemical composition, acknowledging their value in fighting cancer. Acorns (Quercus ilex) are believed to have several unexplored pharmacological properties.

title: 559. Early irritability change in males predicts antidepressant response to DLPFC-rTMS
creator: S Smith, D Blumberger, S Rizvi, W Lou, S Kennedy, K Dunlop
description: BackgroundRepetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is an effective treatment for depression. However, individual responses vary, highlighting the need to identify reliable predictors of treatment outcome. Irritability is a common, understudied symptom that may help predict rTMS outcomes, and examining it by sex may reveal patterns. However, no study has investigated whether early changes in irritability predict rTMS response by sex.

title: Unravelling Eribulin’s role in metastatic breast cancer: evaluating benefits for both triple negative and non-triple negative patients in real-world scenarios in resource-constrained settings
creator: Akhil Kapoor, Anuj Gupta, Bipinesh Sansar, Pooja Gupta, Bal Krishna Mishra, Arpita Singh, Arvind Upadhyay, Amit Kumar, Mayank Tripathi, Zachariah Chowdhury, Shashikant Patne, Ipsita Dhal, Neha Singh, Shreya Shukla, Satyendra Narayan Singh, Lincoln Pujari, Prashanth Giridhar, Ankita Rungta Kapoor, Ya
description: BackgroundMetastatic breast cancer (MBC) patients have numerous options for treatment. However, it is essential to consider treatments with favorable toxicity profiles and convenient modes of administration. Eribulin has shown effectiveness in aggressive MBC, but there is a lack of sufficient real-world data specific to Indian patients.

title: The lived experience of mask wearing among patients with chronic illnesses during the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Parvaneh Aghajari, Mina Hosseinzadeh, Zahra Sheikhalipour
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The COVID-19 pandemic necessitated widespread mask-wearing as a key preventive measure. While masks played a crucial role in limiting virus transmission, their implications for individuals living with chronic illnesses remain underexplored. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences of patients with chronic conditions regarding mask-wearing during and after the COVID-19 pandemic, with a focus on physical, psychological, and social aspects.

title: 210. The role of dorsomedial striatum and parvalbumin interneurons in schizophrenia-related cognitive deficits: insights from disrupted strategic decision-making in Akt1 heterozygous mice
creator: W-S Lai, C-Y Chang, C Chen, Y-W Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSchizophrenia is characterized by pervasive cognitive impairments that emerge early in the illness and strongly predict functional outcomes. Among these deficits, disruptions in decision-making are consistently observed, suggesting abnormalities in reward-learning mechanisms. AKT1, a major schizophrenia susceptibility gene involved in dopamine signaling, shows reduced expression in patients and in Akt1-deficient mouse models, which display altered striatal function and abnormal reward updating.

title: Can back exosuits simultaneously increase lifting endurance and reduce musculoskeletal disorder risk?
creator: KM Rodzak, PR Slaughter, DN Wolf, CC Ice, SJ Fine, KE Zelik
description: The objectives of this case series study were to test whether an elastic back exosuit could increase a wearer’s endurance when lifting heavy objects and to assess whether lifting more cancels out the exosuit’s risk reduction benefits. We found that 88% of participants increased their lifting repetitions while wearing an exosuit, with endurance increases ranging from 28 to 75%.

title: 714. Bipolar disorder: trait and state functional neuroimaging biomarkers
creator: Y Su, Y Wu, T Si
description: BackgroundBipolar disorder (BD) is uniquely characterized by fluctuations of opposing moods (mania/ hypomania and depression) as well as shifts between pathologic and euthymic states. Advances in functional MRI methodologies have helped delineate the functional neuroanatomy associated with BD. Nevertheless, the pathophysiological mechanisms responsible for mood instability, transitions between mood states, and the emergence of extreme mood episodes remain inadequately elucidated.

title: Immature platelet fraction and bone marrow findings in hematology
creator: Satoshi Yamasaki, Michitoshi Hashiguchi, Nao Yoshida-Sakai, Hiroto Jojima, Koichi Osaki, Takashi Okamura, Yutaka Imamura
description: Bone marrow examination (BME) and the assessment of the immature platelet fraction (IPF) are crucial diagnostic tools in hematology. The IPF is the proportion of young, newly released platelets of the total number in the peripheral circulation. We conducted a retrospective study of 1,552 patients with various hematologic disorders, evaluating the relationship between BME findings and IPF.

title: The association of hypokalemia with meropenem administration: A case report and literature review
creator: Abdulmalik Timamy, Eugine Chizooma, Amina Al-Qaysi, Maria Panourgia, Mohamed H Ahmed
description: We report the case of a 72-year-old woman who was admitted following a fall and sustained a right neck of femur fracture. Prior to this admission, she was undergoing chemotherapy for lung cancer. Upon this admission, it was noted that she had developed neutropenic sepsis. She was initially treated with teicoplanin and ciprofloxacin.

title: 420. Neurophysiological and cognitive markers for panic disorder: a multimodal predictive modeling study
creator: S-I Lee, S J Cho, H Lee, J-Y Lee, S Y Yoo
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPanic disorder (PD) is characterized by heightened physiological arousal and disrupted cognitive control, yet its assessment still relies predominantly on subjective self-report scales. Resting-state EEG has been suggested as a promising physiological marker of PD, but findings across frequency bands have been inconsistent, and few studies have integrated EEG with other relevant modalities such as heart rate variability (HRV) and cognitive performance. Moreover, limited work has systematically evaluated these modalities within a unified predictive framework.

title: Advancing the Evidence Base for Tricuspid TEER
creator: Tsz-Ho Chan, Kent Chak-yu So
description: Corresponding AuthorKey words: DragonFly-T, randomized controlled trial, tricuspid regurgitation, transcather edge-to-edge repair The treatment landscape for severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) has evolved dramatically. Once regarded as the “forgotten valve,” TR is now recognized as an independent contributor to heart failure symptoms, impaired quality of life, recurrent hospitalizations, and mortality.

title: Para-Anastomotic Pseudoaneurysms as a Long-Term Complication After Surgical Treatment of Peripheral Artery Disease: Clinical Characteristics and Surgical Treatment
creator: Julia Łacna, Michał Serafin, Dorota Łyko-Morawska, Julia Szostek, Dariusz Stańczyk, Iga Kania, Magdalena Mąka, Waclaw Kuczmik, Jun Lu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is becoming an increasingly prevalent clinical issue, leading to a growing number of patients requiring surgical interventions. Consequently, there is an increasing occurrence of para-anastomotic aneurysms as late complications following primary treatment for PAD. These aneurysms typically arise at the sites of graft implantation and necessitate individualized management strategies based on factors such as location, size, and the patient’s overall condition.

title: The global hydrogen budget
creator: Zutao Ouyang, Robert B Jackson, Marielle Saunois, Josep G Canadell, Yuanhong Zhao, Catherine Morfopoulos, Paul B Krummel, Prabir K Patra, Glen P Peters, Fraser Dennison, Thomas Gasser, Alexander T Archibald, Vivek Arora, Gabriel Baudoin, Naveen Chandra, Philippe Ciais, Steven J Davis, Sarah Feron, F
description: Hydrogen (H2) will play a part in decarbonizing the global energy system1. However, hydrogen interacts with methane, ozone, and stratospheric water vapour, leading to an indirect 100-year global warming potential of 11 ± 4 (refs. 2–5). This raises concerns about the climate consequences of increasing H2 use under future hydrogen economies3,5.

title: miR-24-3p Is Antiviral Against SARS-CoV-2 by Downregulating Critical Host Entry Factors
creator: Parrish Evers, Spencer M. Uguccioni, Nadine Ahmed, Magen E. Francis, Alyson A. Kelvin, John P. Pezacki
description: Despite all the progress in treating SARS-CoV-2, escape mutants to current therapies remain a constant concern. Promising alternative treatments for current and future coronaviruses are those that limit escape mutants by inhibiting multiple pathogenic targets, analogous to the current strategies for treating HCV and HIV.

title: 775. The influence of mindfulness-based nutritional therapy measures on the modification of nutritional problems in patients with psychopathogenic symptoms and implications for psychiatric treatment
creator: C A Penkov, K Friedrich, J Krieger, V Rößner-Ruff, M Becksvoort, M Ziegenbein
description: BackgroundStudies and the S3 practice guidelines in psychiatry and psychotherapy show that health-promoting measures are highly relevant in the treatment of mental illness. Current psychiatric care research still shows ambivalent findings regarding the effects of specific diets on psychopathogenic symptoms.

title: Integrated analysis of post-transcriptional regulations reveals insights into acute myeloid leukemia
creator: Elissa Khadra, Zoaila Iqbal, Morgane Le Gall, Guilhem Clary, Francoise Levavasseur, Zubaidan Tuerdi, Charles Dussiau, David Rombaut, Marie Temple, Chloe Friedrich, Romain Vazquez, Justine Decroocq, Clément Larrue, Didier Bouscary, Olivier Kosmider, Nicolas Chapuis, Yannick Simoni, Jerome Tamburini,
description: Post-transcriptional regulations play crucial roles in gene expression, but their global impact in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains poorly understood. Here, we perform an integrative analysis of transcriptomic and proteomic data from 44 AML samples to uncover the determinants of protein-to-mRNA-ratios (PTRs), a metric summarizing post-transcriptional regulatory processes.

title: Epidemiology of Pertussis After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Analysis of the Factors Involved in the Resurgence of the Disease in High-, Middle-, and Low-Income Countries
creator: Lucia F. Bricks, Juan C. Vargas-Zambrano, Denis Macina
description: Pertussis is a highly contagious bacterial disease of the respiratory tract that can be prevented by vaccination. Before the COVID-19 pandemic, the vaccine coverage rate for the third dose of a DPT-containing vaccine was 86%, with large disparities among countries.

title: 856. Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia: Definitions, Current Pharmacological Strategies, and Emerging Pipeline Therapies
creator: M Samara
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAntipsychotic monotherapy is the guideline-supported mainstay of treatment for schizophrenia. However, approximately 40% of patients fail to achieve an adequate response in randomized controlled trials, highlighting the significant clinical challenge of treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). Despite clozapine being the gold standard for TRS, its use is often limited by concerns over its side effect profile and the need for mandatory blood monitoring.

title: Whole-genome sequencing GWAS reveals bovine genomic effects on enteric methane emissions in beef cattle
creator: Leonardo M Arikawa, Lucio F M Mota, Larissa F S Fonseca, Gerardo A Fernandes Júnior, Sindy L C Nasner, Júlia P S Valente, Tainara L S Soares, Marcelo S Borges, Joel A Silva, Amalia M Pelaez, Maria E Z Mercadante, Lucia G Albuquerque
description: The world has recognized the significance of sustainable animal production, especially in terms of mitigating methane emissions. Developing strategies to mitigate methane without compromising productivity presents a significant challenge for nutritionists and breeders. However, measuring methane emissions at the individual level can be expensive and laborious.

title: Organic Moiety on Sn(IV) Does Matter for In Vitro Mode of Action: nBu3Sn(IV) Compounds with Carboxylato N-Functionalized 2-Quinolones Induce Anoikis-like Cell Death in A375 Cells
creator: Marijana P. Kasalović, Sanja Jelača, Dušan Dimić, Danijela Maksimović-Ivanić, Verica V. Jevtić, Sanja Mijatović, Tobias Rüffer, Goran N. Kaluđerović, Nebojša Đ. Pantelić
description: Objectives: New tributyltin(IV) complexes containing the carboxylate ligands 3-(4-methyl-2-oxoquinolin-1(2H)-yl)propanoic acid (HL1) and 2-(4-methyl-2-oxoquinolin-1(2H)-yl)acetic acid (HL2) have been synthesized. Methods: Their structures have been determined by elemental microanalysis, FT-IR and multinuclear NMR (1H, 13C and 119Sn) spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction study.

title: 440. Acute modulation of cortical excitability by high-dose intermittent theta burst stimulation: a TMS-EEG study
creator: S X Wang, WM W Chau, VW M Lam, TT Z Lin, R R Zeng, M Jin, A W Xia, J J Zhang, G Kranz
description: BackgroundStanford Neuromodulation Therapy (SNT) has achieved rapid remission in treatment-resistant depression through an accelerated, high-dose iTBS schedule. While this implies a cumulative induction of synaptic plasticity, the acute neurophysiological mechanisms of a single session (1800 pulses)—the fundamental building block of this effect—remain elusive.

title: Fragmented QRS duration as a marker of cardiac and hepatic iron overload: across-sectional study
creator: Seyyed Bozorgmehr Hedayati, Soodeh Hooshmandi, Raheb Ghorbani, Mohammad Kamali, Mohammad Hashem Arabkhani
description: Thalassemia is a group of hematological disorders brought about by defective globin chains synthesis, which can indirectly culminate in hepatic and myocardial cellular damages through iron deposition. The purpose of this study is to examine the relationship between fragmented QRS duration and liver T2* value.

title: 834. Bipolar Affective Disorder with Psychodermatological Manifestation: A Clinical Case Illustrating the Neuroimmune Interaction Between Mood Dysregulation and Atopic Dermatitis
creator: K Runtuk, F Putri, I Donoseputro
description: BackgroundBipolar disorder is increasingly conceptualized as a systemic condition involving neurobiological, circadian, and inflammatory dysregulation. Growing evidence suggests shared immunological and stress-related pathways between affective disorders and inflammatory skin diseases such as atopic dermatitis. The brain–skin axis represents a bidirectional interaction in which psychological stress and mood instability may exacerbate dermatologic inflammation, while chronic somatic symptoms may worsen psychiatric outcomes.

title: Oxidative Stress and Keap1-Nrf2 Pathway Involvement in Bisphenol A-Induced Liver Damage in Rats
creator: Juan Tang, Kai Wang, Dan Shen, Chunmei Li, William S Baldwin
description: Bisphenol A (BPA), extensively utilized in the manufacture of epoxy resins and polycarbonate plastics, is prevalent in the environment. Its exposure has been associated with an increased risk of hepatic lesions; however, the underlying mechanisms and the spectrum of its effects remain poorly understood.

title: Physics-based earthquake early warning using distributed acoustic sensing
creator: Shahar Ben-Zeev, Itzhak Lior
description: We present a physics-based point source earthquake early warning system using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) data. All core modules of the system are based on physical principles of wave propagation, and models that describe the earthquake source and far-field ground motion.

title: Investigating the Rhizosphere Fungal Communities of Healthy and Root-Rot-Infected Lycium barbarum in the Tsaidam Basin, China
creator: Guozhen Duan, Guanghui Fan, Jianling Li, Min Liu, Youchao Qi, Tomislav Cernava, Beibei Ge
description: Lycium barbarum is a plant of considerable economic importance in China. However, root rot poses a significant threat to its yield and quality, leading to substantial economic losses. The disparities in rhizosphere soil fungal communities between healthy and root-rot-affected L. barbarum have not been thoroughly explored.

title: 286. Restoration by ketamine metabolites of cognitive and affective prosocial behaviors in a mouse model of depression
creator: R Yokoyama, M Matsumi, S Asano, Y Ago
description: BackgroundThe execution of prosocial behaviors requires the ability to accurately understand and infer others’ affective states. Impairments in prosocial functioning have been shown to be associated with the pathology of several psychiatric disorders. In particular, individuals with depression exhibit reduced cognitive and affective responses to others’ emotions.

title: Appropriateness of Prescribing Transmucosal Immediate-Release Fentanyl in the Emergency Room, During Hospitalization, and at Discharge: A Retrospective Study
creator: Gary Punjabi, Elena Ramírez, Ziyaur Rahman
description: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the appropriateness of transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl (TIRF) prescriptions in a Madrid emergency room during 2019 and 2022, following a 2018 warning about off-label use. Methods: TIRF prescription in the emergency room search yielded 993 patients in 2019 and 1499 in 2022, of which 140 were randomized for the study, 70 in 2019, and 70 in 2022.

title: In-silico identification, characterization and expression analysis of salt overly sensitive-2 (SOS2) gene family in Gossypium hirsutum L. against abiotic stresses
creator: Laraib Iqra, Muhammad Naveed Shahid, Qurban Ali
description: Gossypium hirsutum backbone of economy of many countries; is primarily grown for production of fiber. This is the first genome-wide analysis of GhSOS2 gene family in G. hirsutum. Primary function of SOS2 is ion homeostasis and plays functional role in osmotic stress as well as drought, effecting the development and growth of plant.

title: 634. Implementation of Pharmacogenetics in Psychiatry across the world: the European Continent
creator: R van Westrhenen
description: BackgroundPharmacogenetics (PGx) is a discipline that investigates heritable genetic variation that impacts drug absorption, metabolization and transport of drugs thereby affecting therapy outcome (van Westrhenen et al. Frontiers in Pharmacology 2021). PGx paves the way for more personalised medication prescription, especially for those patients experiencing side effects or lack of desired clinical effect (van Westrhenen et al. 2021,2025).

title: Validation of an in vitro muscle platform to evaluate myogenesis and calcium handling in control and dystrophic human myotubes
creator: Laura Mosqueira-Martín, Carolina Prendes-García, Camila Vesga-Castro, Pablo Marco-Moreno, Ainhoa Irastorza, Ander Izeta, Iratxe Madarieta, Itxaso Martí-Carrera, Jacobo Paredes, Adolfo López de Munain, Ainara Vallejo-Illarramendi
description: Electrical impedance has emerged as a powerful tool for real-time, label-free, and non-invasive monitoring of cellular processes. Here, we employed an impedance-based assay to characterize the myogenic process of control and dystrophic human myoblasts. First, we conducted a comprehensive analysis of control myoblast differentiation, assessing the effects of initial seeding density and various extracellular matrix coatings.

title: Investigating the Potential of Ufasomes Laden with Nintedanib as an Optimized Targeted Lung Nanoparadigm for Accentuated Tackling of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
creator: Heba M Aboud, Adel A Ali, Nada H Mohammed, Ahmed H E Hassan, Eun Joo Roh, Shahira F El Menshawe, Yuping Bao
description: Background/objectives: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a prevalent interstitial lung disease that typically progresses gradually, leading to respiratory failure and ultimately death. IPF can be treated with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor, nintedanib (NTD), owing to its anti-fibrotic properties, which ameliorate the impairment of lung function.

title: 851. A mechanism for PHF21B recognition of H3K36me3
creator: M-L Wong, Q Ma, J Licinio
description: BackgroundWe have recently identified the epigenetic reader PHF21B as a regulator of synaptic plasticity and social memory in mice. The PHF21B gene is located on chromosome 22q13.3, a region that is deleted in Phelan-McDermid syndrome, a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, impaired social communication, and features overlapping with autism spectrum disorder.

title: Laser Fabrication and Performance of Flexible Pressure Sensors with Ridge-Mimicking Spatially Ordered Microstructures
creator: Linjing Wu, Chao Gao, Jincheng Wang, Chen Zhang, Yuzhi Ke, Weidong Wang
description: The proliferation of flexible pressure sensors has generated new demands for high-sensitivity and low-cost sensors. Here, we propose an elegant strategy to address this challenge by taking a ridge-mimicking, gradient-varying, spatially ordered microstructure as the sensing layer, with laser processing and interdigitated electrodes as the upper and lower electrode layers.

title: Circulating microRNAs miR-21-5p, miR-23a-3p and miR-26a-5p reflect clinical and molecular features of aging
creator: Rossella La Grotta, Paolina Crocco, Serena Dato, Giuseppe Passarino, Giuseppina Rose
description: Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are emerging as key regulators of aging and age-related diseases. Among them, the so-called inflammamiRs miR-21-5p, miR-23a-3p, and miR-26a-5p have been repeatedly linked to inflammation, tissue remodelling, and metabolic dysregulation. In this cross-sectional study, we investigated their expression in older adults (65–103 years) to explore associations with frailty, comorbidity, and major clinical and functional indicators of aging.

title: 644. Rebound mania following abrupt discontinuation of oxcarbazepine in bipolar I disorder: a case report
creator: A Margarido, J Freire, C Coelho
description: BackgroundOxcarbazepine is commonly prescribed as a mood stabilizer in bipolar disorder, particularly for manic and mixed episodes. Abrupt discontinuation or rapid dose reduction of mood-stabilizing medications has been associated with rebound mania, defined as the rapid recurrence or worsening of manic symptoms following treatment cessation.

title: Performance and emission interaction analysis of biodiesel–diesel blends with CeO₂ nanoparticles and diethyl ether in a compression ignition engine
creator: Samuel Tamrat, Yared Seifu, Venkata Ramayya Ancha, Rajendiran Gopal, Ramesh Babu Nallamothu
description: This study aimed to evaluate the effect of adding 75 ppm cerium oxide nanoparticles (CeO2 NPs) with 2% diethyl ether (DEE) to castor biodiesel diesel blends on the performance and emissions of a single-cylinder, four-stroke CI engine operated at 80% load across 1700–3000 rpm, revealing that the nano-additive improved brake torque, brake power, thermal efficiency, and reduced carbon monoxide (CO),

title: Advancements in Materials for 3D-Printed Microneedle Arrays: Enhancing Performance and Biocompatibility
creator: Mahmood Razzaghi, Joel Alexander Ninan, Mohsen Akbari
description: The rapid advancement of 3D printing technology has revolutionized the fabrication of microneedle arrays (MNAs), which hold great promise in biomedical applications such as drug delivery, diagnostics, and therapeutic interventions. This review uniquely explores advanced materials used in the production of 3D-printed MNAs, including photopolymer resins, biocompatible materials, and composite resins, designed to improve mechanical properties, biocompatibility, and functional performance.

title: 465. Mood instability as a transdiagnostic predictor of cannabis use in ADHD and depression: a natural language processing analysis of electronic health records from 13,025 adolescents
creator: A Seker, E Bullock, S Chandler, R Patel, D Quattrone, C Colling, E Sonuga-Barke, J Downs
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCannabis use is elevated in youth with depression and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), but drivers of this increase remain underexplored. The self-medication hypothesis suggests cannabis is used by patients for mood regulation, a common difficulty in ADHD and depression.Aims & ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine associations between mood instability and cannabis use in a large, representative clinical cohort of adolescents diagnosed with ADHD and/or depression.MethodNatural language processing (NLP) approaches were utilised to identify references to mood instability and cannabis use in the electronic

title: Hypergravity hinders proper dendritic patterning of a sensory neuron in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans
creator: Je-hyun Moon, Kyoung-hye Yoon, Jin I. Lee
description: Altering gravity force can modify the three-dimensional spatial environment inside living animals that are adapted to earth’s gravity. This may have deleterious effects on biological processes such as developmental patterning that requires proper molecular interactions in a 3D spatial environment.

title: A Spectroscopy Solution for Contactless Conductivity Detection in Capillary Electrophoresis
creator: Tomas Drevinskas, Audrius Maruška, Hirotaka Ihara, Makoto Takafuji, Linas Jonušauskas, Domantas Armonavičius, Mantas Stankevičius, Kristina Bimbiraitė-Survilienė, Elzbieta Skrzydlewska, Ona Ragažinskienė, Yutaka Kuwahara, Shoji Nagaoka, Vilma Kaškonienė, Loreta Kubilienė
description: This paper introduces a novel contactless single-chip detector that utilizes impedance-to-digital conversion technology to measure impedance in the microfluidic channel or capillary format analytical device. The detector is designed to operate similarly to capacitively coupled contactless conductivity detectors for capillary electrophoresis or chromatography but with the added capability of performing frequency sweeps up to 200 kHz.

title: Mitral Regurgitation Phenotype, Coronary Physiology, and Outcomes After Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair
creator: Julian Alexander A. Huibonhoa, Haw-Ruey Hsieh, Ching-Wei Lee, Yi-Lin Tsai, Su-Chan Chen, Tai-Wei Chen, Chun-Chin Chang, Chiao-Po Hsu, Shih-Hsien Sung
description: ts at elevated surgical risk.2, 3, 4 However, outcomes after M-TEER remain heterogeneous and are influenced by the underlying MR phenotype.5,6 Functional MR (FMR) reflects ventricular remodeling and myocardial dysfunction, whereas degenerative MR (DMR) is primarily caused by intrinsic valvular pathology.

title: A framework for reconfigurable production line changeover task planning based on large language model
creator: Jinliang Hou, Li Yan, Hua Qiang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Addressing the issues of manual intervention, low efficiency, and high error rates in the changeover operations of reconfigurable production lines, this paper proposes an automatic changeover task planning framework for reconfigurable production lines based on Large Language Model(LLM).

title: The Selection and Validation of Reference Genes for RT-qPCR Analysis of the Predatory Natural Enemy Orius nagaii (Hemiptera: Anthocoridae)
creator: Chengxing Wang, Zhenjuan Yin, Yu Wang, Yan Liu, Shan Zhao, Xiaoyan Dai, Ruijuan Wang, Long Su, Hao Chen, Li Zheng, Yifan Zhai, Michael Kristensen
description: Simple SummaryA predatory natural enemy insect, Orius nagaii, has been discovered in both the northern and southern regions of China and is extensively utilized for greenhouse vegetable pest management. The precise selection of reference genes is essential for RT-qPCR analysis to elucidate the expression patterns of key genes implicated in the interaction between O. nagaii and its host.

title: 647. Antidepressant efficacy in children and adolescents: a comprehensive patient-level item-based meta-analysis
creator: E Eriksson, A Lisinski, F Hieronymus
description: BackgroundThe possible efficacy of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) and serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) in depressed children and adolescents remains highly controversial, with some arguing that these drugs are virtually devoid of efficacy in non-adults while others advocate an opposite stance.

title: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography angiography assessment of limbal vasculature changes after sclerocorneal vs. corneal cataract incisions
creator: Tatsuaki Amari, Shuichiro Eguchi, Yusuke Oniyanagi, Suguru Nakagawa
description: This prospective cohort study aimed to compare changes in vascular density around sclerocorneal and corneal incisions after cataract surgery using anterior segment optical coherence tomography angiography (AS-OCTA). To this end, 20 patients undergoing cataract surgery were divided into sclerocorneal and corneal (n = 10 each) incision groups. AS-OCTA imaging was performed preoperatively and at multiple intervals postoperatively.

title: Development and Prevention of Biofilm on Cochlear Implants: A Systematic Review
creator: Alexios Tsikopoulos, Konstantinos Tsikopoulos, Konstantinos Sidiropoulos, Gabriele Meroni, Stefanos Triaridis, Lorenzo Drago, Paraskevi Papaioannidou, Steven M Parnes
description: Background and Objectives: Biofilm formation on cochlear implants (CIs) poses a major problem for surgeons, leading to a high incidence of explantation and revision surgery. Therefore, developing appropriate and cost-effective biofilm detection and prevention techniques is of the essence. In this systematic review, we sought to investigate the development of biofilm formation on CIs.

title: 312. Occupational stress: parallel mediation of psychological and physiological pathways from neuroticism to burnout
creator: H S Lee, S-S Park, S-H Lee
description: BackgroundBurnout is a debilitating consequence of chronic occupational stress, yet few studies have simultaneously examined its psychological and physiological pathways.Aims & ObjectivesThis study tested parallel psychological and physiological mechanisms linking neuroticism to occupational burnout using self-report measures and wearable biosignal data.MethodA total of 150 Korean working adults in high-stress occupations completed standardized measures of neuroticism, perceived occupational stress, and burnout.

title: Impact of Lower-Limb Asymmetries on Physical Performance Among Adolescent Female Tennis Players
creator: Nagore Moreno-Apellaniz, Oscar Villanueva-Guerrero, Víctor Emilio Villavicencio-Álvarez, Santiago Calero-Morales, Elena Mainer-Pardos
description: This study aimed to determine the correlation between interlimb asymmetries and physical performance metrics in adolescent female tennis players. Methods: Twenty-five female tennis players (age: 13.29 ± 0.98 years; weight: 52.52 ± 7.31 kg; height: 162.91 ± 6.02 cm) consented to participate in this study.

title: Experimental study of CO2 sequestration and H2 generation potential through mineral carbonation in Saudi red mud
creator: Khaled Al-Azani, Mohamed Gamal Rezk, Ahmed Farid Ibrahim
description: This study examines the potential of Saudi red mud for CO₂ sequestration through mineral carbonation and its concurrent hydrogen generation. Two batch experiments were conducted under neutral (deionized water) and acidic (1 wt% HCl) conditions at elevated temperature and pressure. Under neutral conditions, the interaction between CO₂ and red mud led to measurable mineralization, with approximately 8.

title: Assessment of hepatic steatosis during rat liver regeneration after 70% partial hepatectomy using stereology and MRI-PDFF
creator: Andrea Lund, Uffe Kjaergaard, Lotte Bertelsen, Esben Søvsø Hansen, Katrine Holm Andersen, Steffen Ringgaard, Jens Randel Nyengaard, Christoffer Laustsen, Frank Viborg Mortensen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Partial hepatectomy (PH) is the primary treatment for liver malignancies, leveraging the liver’s regenerative capacity and metabolic potential. Transient hepatic steatosis is a common occurrence following PH. This study aimed to evaluate the utility of MRI-derived proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) for assessing hepatic lipid content in the regenerating rat liver by correlating it with stereological lipid quantification, used as a histological reference standard.

title: 342. Pharmacogenomics in alcohol use disorder: multi-omics meets brain organoids
creator: M-F Ho, C Zhang, H Li, R Weinshilboum
description: BackgroundWe previously conducted an open label acamprosate trial (n=442) in patients with alcohol use disorder (AUD). Acamprosate is an FDA-approved medication for the treatment of AUD, however, only about 50% of patients will respond to acamprosate. To date, no biological measures are utilized to predict response to acamprosate treatment.

title: From Green Chemistry to Healthy Environments: Silver Nanoparticles as a Dual Antioxidant and Antibacterial Agents for Advancing Biomedicine and Sustainable Wastewater Treatment
creator: Hamza Moussa, Sarah Hamid, Amal Mameri, Sabrina Lekmine, Hichem Tahraoui, Mohammed Kebir, Nabil Touzout, Farid Dahmoune, Mohammad Shamsul Ola, Jie Zhang, Abdeltif Amrane, Zicheng Deng, Donglu Shi
description: The green synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using plant extracts is an eco-friendly method with potential for biomedical and environmental applications. This study aims to synthesize silver nanoparticles (SO-AgNPs) using Salvia officinalis L. extract and evaluate their antioxidant and antibacterial properties, positioning them as candidates for applications in sustainable biomedicine and wastewater treatment. S. officinalis L.

title: Investigating the feasibility and safety of transcranial infraslow gray noise stimulation as a potential treatment for generalized anxiety disorder
creator: Cindy van Sleeuwen, Divya Adhia, Paul Glue, Dirk De Ridder
description: Anxiety is a beneficial behavior that assists survival, although when high levels of anxiety persist it can hinder normal functioning. Despite numerous treatment options most individuals with Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD) continue to suffer from the disorder. A novel neuromodulatory treatment that safely and non-invasively alters pathological neural circuitry associated with GAD is required.

title: Mechanistic analysis of flow functions in tertiary enriched gas injection following secondary lean gas injection
creator: Mojtaba Rahmani, Zahed Adak, Mohammad Hossein Ghazanfari, Mobeen Fatemi
description: Significant amounts of residual oil can remain trapped after primary and secondary recovery stages, which can be effectively recovered using tertiary gas injection processes. While tertiary gas injection in water-swept reservoirs has been widely studied, the characterization of tertiary enriched gas injection following secondary lean gas injection remains underexplored.

title: 593. Regulatory mechanism of astrocytic glutamine synthetase expression
creator: M Terunuma, Y Nasu
description: BackgroundGlutamine synthetase (GS) expressed in astrocytes plays an important role for maintaining the amount of extracellular glutamate in the brain. Reduced expression of GS is observed in epilepsy, but the molecular mechanism underlying the control of GS expression and the mechanism of GS reduction in epileptic brain remain elusive.

title: A Comparison of Contractile Properties and Acute Muscle Fatigue Response in Adult Females with Non-Specific Chronic Low Back Pain
creator: Hyungwoo Lee, Seungwon Lee, Chanki Kim, Kyoungkyu Jeon
description: This study examined the erector spinae contractile properties, trunk isokinetic strength, and differences in acute muscle fatigue response after exercise in young females with and without non-specific chronic low back pain (NSCLBP). This study evaluated participants using tensiomyography and isokinetic trunk strength tests.

title: Non-Contact Stable Arterial Pulse Measurement Using mmWave Array Radar
creator: Fanglin Geng, Zhongrui Bai, Hao Zhang, Changyu Liu, Peng Wang, Zhenfeng Li, Lidong Du, Xianxiang Chen, Zhen Fang, Luciano Mescia
description: Pulse signals can serve as important indicators of one’s cardiovascular condition. However, capturing signals with stable morphology using radar under varying measurement periods remains a significant challenge. This paper reports a non-contact arterial pulse measurement method based on mmWave radar, with stable signals achieved through a range–angle focusing algorithm.

title: 172. Cerebrospinal fluid p75 neurotrophin receptor ectodomain differs between Alzheimer’s disease and late-life depression: links to cognition, sleep, and anxiety
creator: W Omori, N Kajitani, M Okada-Tsuchioka, K Itagaki, M Takebayashi
description: BackgroundDifferentiating late-life depression (LLD) from prodromal or early Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is clinically difficult because affective and cognitive symptoms overlap and a subset of LLD patients shows amyloid-β (Aβ) positivity, limiting the specificity of core CSF Aβ/tau biomarkers. The p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) regulates pro-survival and pro-apoptotic signaling.

title: The interferon-inducible MxB large GTPase attenuates hepatitis B virus replication by activating the RIG-I innate immunity signaling pathway
creator: Masazumi Onuki, Jun Inoue, Kotaro Doi, Masashi Ninomiya, Akitoshi Sano, Mio Tsuruoka, Kosuke Sato, Satoko Sawahashi, Keishi Ouchi, Kengo Watanabe, Mark A. McNiven, Atsushi Masamune
description: The innate immune response has been reported to be perturbed by hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection. We hypothesized that the induction of the IFN-inducible dynamin family member, myxovirus resistance protein 2 (MxB), might support an innate immune response against HBV via mitochondrial alterations. The objective of this study was to elucidate the mechanism by which MxB suppresses HBV replication.

title: 186. Effects of a nature-based intervention on cognitive function in older adults with mild cognitive impairment
creator: D H Kim, E K Kwan, Y S Moon
description: BackgroundMild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) represents a high-risk stage for dementia. Pharmacological treatments for MCI have demonstrated limited efficacy and are frequently associated with adverse effects. Despite recent approvals of Donanemab and Lecanemab, their high cost, complex use, and serious side effects limit real-world applicability, highlighting the need for non-pharmacological approaches. Yet few non-pharmacological interventions are accessible in everyday settings.

title: Echocardiographic Assessment of Biventricular Mechanics of Fetuses and Infants of Gestational Diabetic Mothers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Andrea Sonaglioni, Antonino Bruno, Gian Luigi Nicolosi, Stefano Bianchi, Michele Lombardo, Paola Muti
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is the most common complication in pregnancy, representing a serious risk for the mother and fetus. Identifying new biomarkers to ameliorate the screening and improving GDM diagnosis and treatment is crucial. During the last decade, a few studies have used speckle tracking echocardiography (STE) for assessing the myocardial deformation properties of fetuses (FGDM) and infants (IGDM) of GDM women, providing not univocal results.

title: Spectral-spatial feature fusion for real-time facial expression recognition
creator: Jinjing Ma, Yongcheng Lin, Lanmei Qian, Hongfeng You, Tingyu Gao
description: Facial expression recognition (FER), as a critical task in computer vision and affective computing, has gained considerable attention in recent years. However, current methods often suffer from high computational costs and limited capability in extracting key discriminative features. To address these issues, this paper proposes SPAYOLO (Spectral-aware Perception and Aggregation YOLOv8), a novel FER network based on the YOLOv8 architecture.

title: 843. Not all who wander are lost – Might psychedelics alleviate neurodegeneration and depression in dementia?
creator: J Vieira-Andrade, I Marques, M Brito
description: BackgroundSerotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2AR) agonists play a crucial role in multiple cognitive processes, namely executive functions, learning and memory. Owing partly to this, psychedelics such as lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), psilocybin, dimethyltryptamine (DMT), mescaline and ayahuasca might be valuable adjuvants in improving memory deficits and language impairment.

title: Correction: Yang et al. Acute Effects of Percussive Massage Therapy on Thoracolumbar Fascia Thickness and Ultrasound Echo Intensity in Healthy Male Individuals: A Randomized Controlled Trial. Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health 2023, 20, 1073
creator: Chao Yang, Xingyu Huang, Ying Li, Wiraphong Sucharit, Patpiya Sirasaporn, Wichai Eungpinichpong

And the sentence in Section 4. Discussion was corrected as follows: “The mean TLF thickness in the PT and control groups before the intervention was 2.55 mm and 2.63 mm”.

title: Pathogenic variants in affected and unaffected individuals from Indonesian familial cancer: a multigene panel analysis
creator: Muflihatul Muniroh, Christina Hari Nawangsih Prihharsanti, Edward Kurnia Setiawan Limijadi, Yan Wisnu Prajoko, Yusril Ichzana, Ziyadatun Nabila, Putri Setyawati, Reza Tri Sutrisno, Ermawan Teguh, Ahmad Rusdan H Utomo
description: The precise prevalence of pathogenic gene variants in high or moderate penetrance genes associated with hereditary cancer in Indonesia remains undetermined. Furthermore, the criteria for prioritizing individuals for genetic testing are not well-defined. This study examined gene variants in Indonesian familial cancer among both affected and unaffected individuals.

title: Chinese TEER Innovation
creator: Yunpeng Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026).
