When the impurities are switched into a negatively charged state by the STM tip, periodic charge modulations emerge around the impurity center, but strictly confined by the nanoscale impurity potential.

title: Shared Multi-modal Embedding Space for Face-Voice Association
creator: Christopher Simic, Korbinian Riedhammer, Tobias Bocklet
description: Abstract The FAME 2026 challenge comprises two demanding tasks: training face–voice associations combined with a multilingual setting that includes testing on languages on which the model was not trained. Our approach consists of separate uni-modal processing pipelines with general face and voice feature extraction, complemented by additional age-gender feature extraction to support prediction.

title: Long-term X-ray variability of the multiple-planet host L 98-59: Hints of an activity cycle.
creator: I. Pillitteri, S. Bellotti, S. Benatti, S. Boro Saikia, A. García Muñoz, K. G. Kislyakova, A. Maggio, G. Micela, K. Vida, A. A. Vidotto
description: Abstract High-energy irradiation in X-rays and UV (XUV) can transform the planetary atmospheres through photoevaporation and photochemistry. This is more crucial for M stars, whose habitable zones for Earth-like planets are located within a few percent of an AU. Transiting exoplanets around M dwarfs offer the opportunity to study their characteristics and habitability conditions.

title: DaLA: Danish Linguistic Acceptability Evaluation Guided by Real World Errors
creator: Gianluca Barmina, Nathalie Carmen Hau Norman, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech
description: Abstract We present an enhanced benchmark for evaluating linguistic acceptability in Danish. We first analyze the most common errors found in written Danish. Based on this analysis, we introduce a set of fourteen corruption functions that generate incorrect sentences by systematically introducing errors into existing correct Danish sentences.

title: MOVE: A Simple Motion-Based Data Collection Paradigm for Spatial Generalization in Robotic Manipulation
creator: Huanqian Wang, Chi Bene Chen, Yang Yue, Danhua Tao, Tong Guo, Shaoxuan Xie, Denghang Huang, Shiji Song, Guocai Yao, Gao Huang
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Huanqian Wang, Chi Bene Chen, Yang Yue, Danhua Tao, Tong Guo, Shaoxuan Xie, Denghang Huang, Shiji Song, Guocai Yao, Gao Huang. Imitation learning method has shown immense promise for robotic manipulation, yet its practical deployment is fundamentally constrained by the data scarcity. Despite prior work on collecting large-scale datasets, there still remains a significant gap to robust spatial generalization. We identify a key limitation: individual trajectories, regardless of their length, are typically collected from a single, static spatial configuration of the environment.

title: SIMA 2: A Generalist Embodied Agent for Virtual Worlds
creator: SIMA Team, Google DeepMind
description: Abstract We introduce SIMA 2, a generalist embodied agent that understands and acts in a wide variety of 3D virtual worlds. Built upon a Gemini foundation model, SIMA 2 represents a significant step toward active, goal-directed interaction within an embodied environment. Unlike prior work ( e.g.

title: 287,872 Supermassive Black Holes Masses: Deep Learning Approaching Reverberation Mapping Accuracy
creator: Yuhao Lu, HengJian SiTu, Jie Li, Yixuan Li, Yang Liu, Wenbin Lin, Yu Wang
description: Abstract We present a population-scale catalogue of 287,872 supermassive black hole masses with high accuracy. Using a deep encoder-decoder network trained on optical spectra with reverberation-mapping (RM) based labels of 849 quasars and applied to all SDSS quasars up to z = 4 z=4 , our method achieves a root-mean-square error of 0.058 0.

title: Teaching a Transformer to Think Like a Chemist: Predicting Nanocluster Stability
creator: João Marcos T. Palheta, Octavio Rodrigues Filho, Mohammad Soleymanibrojeni, Alexandre Cavalheiro Dias, Diego Guedes-Sobrinho, Wolfgang Wenzel, Roland Aydin, Celso R. C. Rêgo, Maurício Jeomar Piotrowski
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by João Marcos T. Palheta, Octavio Rodrigues Filho, Mohammad Soleymanibrojeni, Alexandre Cavalheiro Dias, Diego Guedes-Sobrinho, Wolfgang Wenzel, Roland Aydin, Celso R. C. Rêgo, Maurício Jeomar Piotrowski. Atomically precise metal nanoclusters bridge the molecular and bulk regimes, but designing bimetallic motifs with targeted stability and reactivity remains challenging.

title: YingMusic-SVC: Real-World Robust Zero-Shot Singing Voice Conversion with Flow-GRPO and Singing-Specific Inductive Biases
creator: Gongyu Chen, Xiaoyu Zhang, Zhenqiang Weng, Junjie Zheng, Da Shen, Chaofan Ding, Wei-Qiang Zhang, Zihao Chen, [4pt] AI Lab, GiantNetwork
description: Abstract Singing voice conversion (SVC) aims to render the target singer’s timbre while preserving melody and lyrics. However, existing zero-shot SVC systems remain fragile in real songs due to harmony interference, F0 errors, and the lack of inductive biases for singing. We propose YingMusic-SVC, a robust zero-shot framework that unifies continuous pre-training, robust supervised fine-tuning, and Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning.

title: LatentFM: A Latent Flow Matching Approach for Generative Medical Image Segmentation
creator: Trinh Ngoc Huynh, Nguyen Kim Hoang Anh, Nguyen Hai Toan, Tran Quoc Long
description: Abstract Generative models have achieved remarkable progress with the emergence of flow matching (FM). It has demonstrated strong generative capabilities and attracted significant attention as a simulation-free flow-based framework capable of learning exact data densities. Motivated by these advances, we propose LatentFM, a flow-based model operating in the latent space for medical image segmentation.

title: RobustSplat++: Decoupling Densification, Dynamics, and Illumination for In-the-Wild 3DGS PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
creator: Chuanyu Fu, Guanying Chen, Yuqi Zhang, Kunbin Yao, Yuan Xiong, Chuan Huang
description: Abstract 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has gained significant attention for its real-time, photo-realistic rendering in novel-view synthesis and 3D modeling. However, existing methods struggle with accurately modeling in-the-wild scenes affected by transient objects and illuminations, leading to artifacts in the rendered images.

title: Construction of the Nearest Nonnegative Hankel Matrix for a Prescribed Eigenpair
creator: Prince Kanhya, Udit Raj
description: Abstract We study the problem of determining whether a prescribed eigenpair ( λ , x ) (\lambda,x) can be made an exact eigenpair of a nonnegative Hankel matrix through the smallest possible structured perturbation. The task reduces to check the feasibility of a set of linear constraints that encode both the Hankel structure and entrywise nonnegativity.

title: Edge spin galvanic effect in altermagnets
creator: L. E. Golub
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by L. E. Golub. The edge spin galvanic effect (ESGE) in d d -wave altermagnets is proposed. ESGE is a creation of an electrical current flowing along the edge of the sample, which is driven by the spin orientation of charge carriers. The ESGE current is formed owing to the altermagnetic spin splitting and the scattering of carriers by the edge of the sample. The current is sensitive to the orientation of the edge in respect to the main axes of the altermagnet.

title: Contract-Driven QoE Auditing for Speech and Singing Services: From MOS Regression to Service Graphs
creator: Wenzhang Du
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wenzhang Du. Subjective mean opinion scores (MOS) remain the de-facto target for non-intrusive speech and singing quality assessment. However, MOS is a scalar that collapses heterogeneous user expectations, ignores service-level objectives, and is difficult to compare across deployment graphs. We propose a contract-driven QoE auditing framework: each service graph G G is evaluated under a set of human-interpretable experience contracts 𝒞 \mathcal{C} , yielding a contract-level satisfaction vector Q ⁡ ( G , 𝒞 ) Q(G,\mathcal{C}) .

title: Setting up for failure: automatic discovery of the neural mechanisms of cognitive errors
creator: Puria Radmard, Paul M. Bays, Máté Lengyel, [5pt] Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge
description: Abstract Discovering the neural mechanisms underpinning cognition is one of the grand challenges of neuroscience. However, previous approaches for building models of recurrent neural network (RNN) dynamics that explain behaviour required iterative refinement of architectures and/or optimization objectives, resulting in a piecemeal, and mostly heuristic, human-in-the-loop process.

title: Constrained Control of PDE Traffic Flow via Spatial Control Barrier Functions
creator: Brian Block, Stephanie Stockar
description: Abstract In this paper, a constrained control approach to variable speed limit (VSL) control for macroscopic partial differential equation (PDE) traffic models is developed. Control Lyapunov function (CLF) theory for ordinary differential equations (ODEs) is extended to account for spatially and temporally varying states and control inputs.

title: Are LLMs Truly Multilingual? Exploring Zero-Shot Multilingual Capability of LLMs for Information Retrieval: An Italian Healthcare Use Case
creator: Vignesh Kumar Kembu, Pierandrea Morandini, Marta Bianca Maria Ranzini, Antonino Nocera
description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a key topic in AI and NLP, transforming sectors like healthcare, finance, education, and marketing by improving customer service, automating tasks, providing insights, improving diagnostics, and personalizing learning experiences. Information extraction from clinical records is a crucial task in digital healthcare.

title: Hybrid VQE-CVQE algorithm using diabatic state preparation
creator: John P. T. Stenger, C. Stephen Hellberg, Daniel Gunlycke
description: Abstract We propose a hybrid variational quantum algorithm that has variational parameters used by both the quantum circuit and the subsequent classical optimization. Similar to the Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE), this algorithm applies a parameterized unitary operator to the qubit register. We generate this operator using diabatic state preparation.

title: Optimal Transport Event Representation for Anomaly Detection
creator: Aditya Bhargava, Tianji Cai, Benjamin Nachman
description: Abstract We introduce optimal transport (OT) as a physics-based intermediate event representation for weakly supervised anomaly detection. With only 0.5 % 0.5\% injection of resonant signals in the LHC Olympics benchmark datasets, the OT-augmented feature set achieves nearly twice the significance improvement of standard high-level observables, while end-to-end deep learning on low-level four-momenta struggles in the low-signal regime.

title: Time-periodic solutions to an energy balance model coupled with an active fluid under arbitrary large forces
creator: Gianmarco Del Sarto, Matthias Hieber, Filippo Palma, Tarek Zöchling
description: Abstract . This article concerns time-periodic solutions to a two-dimensional Sellers-type energy balance model coupled to the three-dimensional primitive equations via a dynamic boundary condition. It is shown that the underlying equations admit at least one strong time-periodic solution, provided the forcing term is time-periodic.

title: Clustering country-level all-cause mortality data: a review
creator: Pedro M. De Araújo, Isobel Claire Gormley, Thomas Brendan Murphy
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pedro M. De Araújo, Isobel Claire Gormley, Thomas Brendan Murphy. Mortality data are relevant to demography, public health, and actuarial science. Whilst clustering is increasingly used to explore patterns in such data, no study has reviewed its application to country-level all-cause mortality. This review therefore summarises recent work and addresses key questions: why clustering is used, which mortality data are analysed, which methods are most common, and what main findings emerge.

title: Interplay between Superconductivity and Altermagnetism in Disordered Materials and Heterostructures
creator: Rodrigo de las Heras, Tim Kokkeler, Stefan Ilić, Ilya V. Tokatly, F. Sebastian Bergeret
description: Abstract We study the interplay between superconductivity and altermagnetism in disordered systems using recently derived quantum kinetic transport equations. Starting from this framework, we derive the Ginzburg–Landau free energy and identify, in addition to the conventional pair-breaking term, a coupling between the spin and the spatial variation of the superconducting order parameter. Two distinct effects emerge from this coupling.

title: DAMASHA : D etecting A I in M ixed A dversarial Texts via S egmentation with H uman-interpretable A ttribution
creator: L. D. M. S. Sai Teja N. Siva Gopala Krishna Ufaq Khan, Muhammad Haris Khan Partha Pakray Atul Mishra
description: Abstract In the age of advanced large language models (LLMs), the boundaries between human and AI-generated text are becoming increasingly blurred. We address the challenge of segmenting mixed-authorship text, that is identifying transition points in text where authorship shifts from human to AI or vice-versa, a problem with critical implications for authenticity, trust, and human oversight.

title: A Sanity Check for Multi-In-Domain Face Forgery Detection in the Real World
creator: Jikang Cheng, Renye Yan, Zhiyuan Yan, Yaozhong Gan, Xueyi Zhang, Zhongyuan Wang, Wei Peng, Ling Liang, [0.2cm] Peking University, Nanjing University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen
description: Abstract Existing methods for deepfake detection aim to develop generalizable detectors. Although “generalizable” is the ultimate target once and for all, with limited training forgeries and domains, it appears idealistic to expect generalization that covers entirely unseen variations, especially given the diversity of real-world deepfakes. Therefore, introducing large-scale multi-domain data for training can be feasible and important for real-world applications.

title: Typing Fallback Functions: A Semantic Approach to Type Safe Smart Contracts DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: ???; ???; ??? ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06
creator: Stian Lybech, Daniele Gorla, Luca Aceto
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Stian Lybech, Daniele Gorla, Luca Aceto. This paper develops semantic typing in a smart-contract setting to ensure type safety of code that uses statically untypable language constructs, such as the fallback function. The idea is that the creator of a contract on the blockchain equips code containing such constructs with a formal proof of its type safety, given in terms of the semantics of types.

title: Language Models as Semantic Teachers: Post-Training Alignment for Medical Audio Understanding
creator: Tsai - Ning Wang, Lin - Lin Chen, Neil Zeghidour, Aaqib Saeed
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tsai - Ning Wang, Lin - Lin Chen, Neil Zeghidour, Aaqib Saeed. Pre-trained audio models excel at detecting acoustic patterns in auscultation sounds but often fail to grasp their clinical significance, limiting their use and performance in diagnostic tasks.

title: io _ uring for High-Performance DBMSs: When and How to Use It
creator: Matthias Jasny, Muhammad El-Hindi, Tobias Ziegler, Viktor Leis, Carsten Binnig
description: Abstract . We study how modern database systems can leverage the Linux io _ uring interface for efficient, low-overhead I/O. io _ uring is an asynchronous system call batching interface that unifies storage and network operations, addressing limitations of existing Linux I/O interfaces. However, naively replacing traditional I/O interfaces with io _ uring does not necessarily yield performance benefits.

title: Contact-Aware Refinement of Human Pose Pseudo-Ground Truth via Bioimpedance Sensing
creator: Maria-Paola Forte, Nikos Athanasiou, Giulia BallardiniJan Ulrich BartelsKatherine J. KuchenbeckerMichael J. Black Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, Stuttgart and Tübingen, Germany {forte,ballardini,jub,kjk}@is.mpg.de{nikos.athanasiou,black}@tue.mpg.de
description: Abstract Capturing accurate 3D human pose in the wild would provide valuable data for training pose estimation and motion generation methods. While video-based estimation approaches have become increasingly accurate, they often fail in common scenarios involving self-contact, such as a hand touching the face. In contrast, wearable bioimpedance sensing can cheaply and unobtrusively measure ground-truth skin-to-skin contact.

title: Searching for new physics with 136 Xe double beta decay spectrum in PandaX-4T
creator: Zhe Yuan, Zihao Bo, Wei Chen, Xun Chen, Yunhua Chen, Chen Cheng, Xiangyi Cui, Manna Deng, Yingjie Fan, Deqing Fang, Xuanye Fu, Zhixing Gao, Yujie Ge, Lisheng Geng, Karl Giboni, Xunan Guo, Xuyuan Guo, Zichao Guo, Chencheng Han, Ke Han, Changda He, Jinrong He, Houqi Huang, Junting Huang, Yule Huang, R
description: Abstract The continuous spectrum of double beta decay ( β ​ β \beta\beta ) provides a sensitive probe to test the predictions of the Standard Model and to search for signatures of new physics beyond it. We present a comprehensive analysis of the 136 Xe β ​ β \beta\beta spectrum utilizing 37.8 ± 0.6 37.8\pm 0.

title: Safe model-based Reinforcement Learning via Model Predictive Control and Control Barrier Functions
creator: Kerim Dzhumageldyev, Filippo Airaldi, Azita Dabiri
description: Abstract Optimal control strategies are often combined with safety certificates to ensure both performance and safety in safety-critical systems. A prominent example is combining Model Predictive Control (MPC) with Control Barrier Functions (CBF). Yet, efficient tuning of MPC parameters and choosing an appropriate class 𝒦 \mathcal{K} function in the CBF is challenging and problem dependent.

title: Counterfactual Explanations for Power System Optimisation
creator: Benjamin Fritz, Waqquas Bukhsh
description: Abstract Enhanced computational capabilities of modern decision-making software have allowed us to solve increasingly sophisticated optimisation problems. But in complex socio-economic, technical environments such as electricity markets, transparent operation is key to ensure a fair treatment of all parties involved, particularly regarding dispatch decisions.

title: Detecting relativistic black hole collisions near a massive black hole
creator: Yirong Fang, Changfu Shi, Jianwei Mei
description: Abstract Relativistic black hole collisions are one of the most dramatic astrophysical events that can be imagined. They could provide the ideal condition for searching for possible new physics beyond general relativity. However, such events are presumably rare and difficult to occur under normal conditions.

title: Pion physics with dressed quark-gluon vertices
creator: M.N. Ferreira, A.S. Miramontes, J.M. Morgado, J. Papavassiliou, J.M. Pawlowski
description: Abstract Recently, a theoretical framework was set up in Miramontes et al. 2025a , which allows for the symmetry-preserving inclusion of full quark-gluon vertices in the description of the meson dynamics. In the present work, we develop a special truncation within this approach, which leads to a tractable set of functional equations that satisfy the fundamental chiral Ward-Takahashi identities.

title: Are Your Agents Upward Deceivers?
creator: Dadi Guo, Qingyu Liu, Dongrui Liu, Qihan Ren, Shuai Shao, Tianyi Qiu, Haoran Li, Yi R. Fung, Zhongjie Ba, Juntao Dai, Jiaming Ji, Zhikai Chen, Jialing Tao, Yaodong Yang, Jing Shao, Xia Hu
description: Abstract Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous subordinates that carry out tasks for users. This raises the question of whether they may also engage in deception, similar to how individuals in human organizations lie to superiors to create a good image or avoid punishment.

title: SP-Det: Self-Prompted Dual-Text Fusion for Generalized Multi-Label Lesion Detection Journal: Knowledge-Based Systems
creator: Qing Xu †,, Yanqian Wang †,, Xiangjian He, Yue Li, Yixuan Zhang, Rong Qu, Wenting Duan, Zhen Chen
description: Abstract Automated lesion detection in chest X-rays has demonstrated significant potential for improving clinical diagnosis by precisely localizing pathological abnormalities. While recent promptable detection frameworks have achieved remarkable accuracy in target localization, existing methods typically rely on manual annotations as prompts, which are labor-intensive and impractical for clinical applications.

title: Chameleon: Adaptive Adversarial Agents for Scaling-Based Visual Prompt Injection in Multimodal AI Systems Thanks:
creator: M Zeeshan, Saud Satti
description: Abstract Multimodal Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems, particularly Vision-Language Models (VLMs), have become integral to critical applications ranging from autonomous decision-making to automated document processing. As these systems scale, they rely heavily on preprocessing pipelines to handle diverse inputs efficiently. However, this dependency on standard preprocessing operations, specifically image downscaling, creates a significant yet often overlooked security vulnerability.

title: Optical Readout of Reconfigurable Layered Magnetic Domain Structure in CrSBr
creator: Aleksandra Łopion, Pierre-Maurice Piel, Manuel Terbeck, Jan-Hendrik Larusch, Jakob Henz, Marie-Christin Heißenbüttel, Kseniia Mosina, Thorsten Deilmann, Michael Rohlfing, Zdenek Sofer, Ursula Wurstbauer
description: Abstract The emergence of intelligent matter has sparked significant interest in next–generation technologies. We report on the discovery of a reconfigurable magnetic multilayer domain structure in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr, exhibiting a unique combination of magnetic and optical properties.

title: Logic-Driven Cybersecurity: A Novel Framework for System Log Anomaly Detection using Answer Set Programming
creator: Fang Li, Fei Zuo, Gopal Gupta
description: Abstract This study explores the application of Answer Set Programming (ASP) for detecting anomalies in system logs, addressing the challenges posed by evolving cyber threats. We propose a novel framework that leverages ASP’s declarative nature and logical reasoning capabilities to encode complex security rules as logical predicates.

title: FENCE: Flexible Electric Noise Cancellation Endo-shield for the Suppression of Electromagnetic Interference in Low-Field MRI
creator: Julia Pfitzer, Martin Uecker, Hermann Scharfetter
description: Abstract Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a significant challenge for low-field MRI systems operating without conventional Faraday-shielded rooms. This interference degrades image quality and limits deployment in space-constrained or electromagnetically noisy environments. Traditional EMI mitigation approaches include external shields, subject grounding via electrodes, or active noise cancellation requiring synchronized receive channels.

title: PVLS: A Learning-Based Parameter Prediction Technique for Variational Quantum Linear Solvers Journal: Pattern Recognition Letters
creator: Youla Yang, Chi Zhang, Lei Jiang
description: Abstract Variational quantum linear solvers (VQLSs) are a promising class of hybrid quantum–classical algorithms for solving linear systems on near-term quantum devices. However, the performance of VQLSs is often impeded by barren plateaus, particularly when using randomly initialized variational quantum circuits (VQCs).

title: Instantons meet resonances: Unifying two seemingly distinct approaches to quantum tunneling
creator: Björn Garbrecht, Nils Wagner
description: Abstract In the study of quantum-mechanical tunneling processes, numerous approaches have been developed to determine the decay rate of states initially confined within a metastable potential region. Virtually all analytical treatments, however, fall into one of two superficially unrelated conceptual frameworks: the resonant-state approach and the instanton method.

title: Torsion and complete dualizable objects in tensor-triangulated categories over a Noetherian ring Thanks: The research was supported by the Czech Science Foundation grant GA ČR 23-05148S
creator: Jun Maillard and Jan Šťovíček
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Jun Maillard and Jan Šťovíček. We study categories of dualizable torsion and complete objects for compactly-rigidly generated tensor-triangulated categories 𝖳 \mathsf{T} with a Noetherian central action of a graded commutative Noetherian ring R R .

title: Hoi! - A Multimodal Dataset for Force-Grounded, Cross-View Articulated Manipulation
creator: Tim Engelbracht, René Zurbrügg, Matteo Wohlrapp, Martin Büchner, Abhinav Valada, Marc Pollefeys, Hermann Blum, Zuria Bauer
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tim Engelbracht, René Zurbrügg, Matteo Wohlrapp, Martin Büchner, Abhinav Valada, Marc Pollefeys, Hermann Blum, Zuria Bauer. We present a dataset for force-grounded, cross-view articulated manipulation that couples what is seen with what is done and what is felt during real human interaction. The dataset contains 3048 sequences across 381 articulated objects in 38 environments. Each object is operated under four embodiments - (i) human hand, (ii) human hand with a wrist-mounted camera, (iii) handheld UMI gripper, and (iv) a custom Hoi!

title: On Disturbance-Aware Minimum-Time Trajectory Planning: Evidence from Tests on a Dynamic Driving Simulator
creator: Matteo Masoni, Vincenzo Palermo, Marco Gabiccini, Martino Gulisano, Giorgio Previati, Massimiliano Gobbi, Francesco Comolli, Gianpiero Mastinu, Massimo Guiggiani
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Matteo Masoni, Vincenzo Palermo, Marco Gabiccini, Martino Gulisano, Giorgio Previati, Massimiliano Gobbi, Francesco Comolli, Gianpiero Mastinu, Massimo Guiggiani. This work aims to investigate how disturbance-aware, robustness-embedding reference trajectories translate into actual driving performance when executed by professional drivers in a dynamic driving simulator.

title: Cute but Cunning: Effective Closed-Form Alternatives to the Exact Lognormal Statistics
creator: Carlos Rafael Nogueira da Silva, Maria Cecilia Luna Alvarado, Fernando Darío Almeida García, and Michel Daoud Yacoub
description: Abstract The Lognormal distribution is a fundamental statistical model widely used in different fields of science, including biology, finance, economics, engineering, etc. In wireless communications, it is the primary statistic for large-scale fading modeling. However, its known analytical intractability presents persistent channel characterization and performance analysis challenges.

title: Toward Continuous Neurocognitive Monitoring: Integrating Speech AI with Relational Graph Transformers for Rare Neurological Diseases
creator: Raquel Norel, Michele Merler, Pavitra Modi
description: Abstract . Patients with rare neurological diseases report cognitive symptoms—“brain fog”—invisible to traditional tests. We propose continuous neurocognitive monitoring via smartphone speech analysis integrated with Relational Graph Transformer (RELGT) architectures. Proof-of-concept in phenylketonuria (PKU) shows speech-derived “Proficiency in Verbal Discourse” correlates with blood phenylalanine ( ρ = − 0.50 \rho=-0.50 , p < 0.005 p<0.

creator: Clara Zyskind, Thomas Lauprêtre, Haosen Shang, Benjamin Pointard, Rodolphe Le Targat, Jérôme Lodewyck, Sébastien Bize

title: Shorting Dynamics and Structured Kernel Regularization
creator: James Tian
description: Abstract . This paper develops a nonlinear operator dynamic that progressively removes the influence of a prescribed feature subspace while retaining maximal structure elsewhere. The induced sequence of positive operators is monotone, admits an exact residual decomposition, and converges to the classical shorted operator.

title: The AI Consumer Index (ACE)
creator: Julien Benchek, Rohit Shetty, Benjamin Hunsberger, Ajay Arun, Zach Richards, Brendan Foody, Osvald Nitski, Bertie Vidgen
description: Abstract We introduce the first version of the AI Consumer Index (ACE), a benchmark for assessing whether frontier AI models can perform everyday consumer tasks. ACE contains a hidden heldout set of 400 400 test cases, split across four consumer activities: shopping, food, gaming, and DIY.

title: Equivariant Symmetry-Aware Head Pose Estimation for Fetal MRI
creator: Ramya Muthukrishnan, Borjan Gagoski, Aryn Lee, P. Ellen Grant, Elfar Adalsteinsson, Polina Golland, Benjamin Billot
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ramya Muthukrishnan, Borjan Gagoski, Aryn Lee, P. Ellen Grant, Elfar Adalsteinsson, Polina Golland, Benjamin Billot. We present E(3)-Pose, a novel fast pose estimation method that jointly and explicitly models rotation equivariance and object symmetry. Our work is motivated by the challenging problem of accounting for fetal head motion during a diagnostic MRI scan. We aim to enable automatic adaptive prescription of 2D diagnostic MRI slices with 6-DoF head pose estimation, supported by 3D MRI volumes rapidly acquired before each 2D slice.

title: Towards Adaptive Fusion of Multimodal Deep Networks for Human Action Recognition
creator: Novanto Yudistira
description: Abstract This study introduces a pioneering methodology for human action recognition by harnessing deep neural network techniques and adaptive fusion strategies across multiple modalities, including RGB, optical flows, audio, and depth information. Employing gating mechanisms for multimodal fusion, we aim to surpass limitations inherent in traditional unimodal recognition methods while exploring novel possibilities for diverse applications.

title: The Spacetime Penrose Inequality: Conditional Results for Stable MOTS and General Trapped Surfaces
creator: Da Xu
description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Da Xu. We present a rigorous proof of the Spacetime Penrose Inequality relating the ADM mass to the area of trapped surfaces in asymptotically flat initial data sets satisfying the dominant energy condition. The main theorem establishes that the ADM mass is bounded below by the square root of the area divided by 16 pi for an area-maximizing marginally outer trapped surface (MOTS), subject to a distributional favorable jump condition which we prove is structurally guaranteed by KKT optimality.

title: Next-order asymptotics for the volume of Schatten balls
creator: Mathias Sonnleitner
description: Abstract . The volume of the unit balls of self-adjoint finite-dimensional Schatten p p -classes of n × n n\times n -matrices, 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ 1\leq p\leq\infty , is only known exactly for p = 2 p=2 and p = ∞ p=\infty .

title: Oxygen Isotope Constraints on the Importance of Photochemical Processing in Protoplanetary Disks CANDY ( E. V. Clepper et al. 2022 ) astrochem ( S. Maret & E. A. Bergin 2015 ) matplotlib ( J. D. Hunter 2007 ) numpy ( C. R. Harris et al. 2020 )
creator: Fred J. Ciesla, Eric Van Clepper, Jennifer Bergner, Edwin Bergin
description: Abstract Observations have revealed evidence of photochemical processing in protoplanetary disks. This processing occurs in the photon dominated layer, the optically thin regions of the disk high above the disk midplane. It remains unclear, however, how much this photochemical processing impacts the compositions of the planets and their building blocks within the disk.

creator: Dylan Magill 1, M. Nicholl 1, V. Anilkumar 2, S. van Velzen 2, X. Sheng 1, \newauthor T. S. Mai 3, H. V. Tran 3, N. P. Doan 3, T. Moore 1,4, S. Srivastav 5, \newauthor D. R. Young 1, C. R.
