description: INTRODUCTIONZolbetuximab, a monoclonal antibody targeting claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), has recently demonstrated significant survival benefits when combined with chemotherapy for advanced gastric cancer. However, evidence regarding conversion surgery following SOX plus zolbetuximab therapy remains extremely limited.CASE PRESENTATIONA 59-year-old woman presented with epigastric discomfort. Endoscopy revealed a depressed lesion in the lower gastric body, and biopsy confirmed signet-ring cell carcinoma.

title: Predictive Performance of a Serum sRAGE/sVEGFR-3 Dual-Biomarker Combination for Hypercoagulability Status in Pediatric Mycoplasma pneumoniae Pneumonia: A Retrospective Cohort Analysis
creator: Chunzhe Guo, Fang Cheng, Shixin Sun, Lina Kang, Gaoyin Zhang, Hong An
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate serum soluble receptor for advanced glycation end products (sRAGE) and soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 3 (sVEGFR-3) as biomarkers for hypercoagulable state in children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP).MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled 352 children with MPP (hypercoagulable, n=98; non-hypercoagulable, n=254). Serum sRAGE and sVEGFR-3 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

title: Complete Skin Clearance is Associated with HADS-Defined Absence of Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms After IL-17A Inhibitor Treatment in Moderate-to-Severe Psoriasis: Evidence from the SPEECH Cohort
creator: Zhenquan Xuan, Yingbao Zhen, Didaer Muheyati, Dawei Huang, Lian Cui, Zeyu Chen, Min Dai, Yuxiong Jiang, Yangfeng Ding, Qian Yu, Yuling Shi
description: BackgroundPsoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated disease associated with anxiety, depressive symptoms, and impaired quality of life, potentially involving interacting psychosocial and inflammatory pathways. During biologic treatment, psychological symptoms may improve alongside skin disease, but whether complete skin clearance (CSC) is associated with Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS)-defined absence of anxiety and depressive symptoms remains unclear.

title: Self-Fitting Versus Professional-Fitting Hearing Aids: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
creator: Ebraheem Albazee, Hajar Alismail, Noof Albannai, Yaqoub Yousef Alenezi, Abdullah M. Alharran, Maya Yassir H. Ibrahim, Durar Ahmed Aljishi, Ahmed Abu-Zaid
description: Background: Adult hearing loss is common, yet hearing-aid uptake remains inadequate due to systemic and financial barriers in traditional audiologist-based fitting models. Over-the-counter (OTC) and self-fitting strategies have emerged to improve accessibility, allowing users to select and adjust their devices independently. However, concerns remain that reducing professional involvement may compromise electroacoustic accuracy, speech-in-noise outcomes, and overall patient satisfaction.

title: Melatonin potentiates the antineoplastic effects of venetoclax in acute myeloid leukemia cells
creator: Vahid Vahedian, Keli Lima, Bruna Oliveira de Almeida, Rita de Cássia Cavaglieri, João Agostinho Machado-Neto, Eduardo Magalhães Rego
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). e disease predominantly affects older adults and remains associated with poor clinical outcomes, particularly in patients who are unfit for intensive chemotherapy due to comorbidities and adverse-risk disease biology [2]. Despite standard myelosuppressive chemotherapy approaches, including anthracycline-cytarabine-based induction and consolidation with or without allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, relapse rates remain high, largely due to the persistence of therapy-resistant leukemic stem cells or clonal evolution or both [3].

title: Anxiety and Depressive Symptoms Among Early‐Year Medical Students in Pakistan: Prevalence, Associated Factors, and Mental Health Service Implications—A Multicenter Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Farah Rashid, Iffat Noor, Wajeha Najeeb, Hadiya Rashed Siddiqui, Hafiz Muhammad Ali, Abid Malik, Atif Rahman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAnxiety and depressive symptoms are common among medical students, but multicenter evidence from the early years of training in Pakistan is limited. We estimated symptom prevalence and examined sociodemographic, behavioral, academic, and psychosocial correlates of symptom severity.MethodsWe conducted a multicenter cross‐sectional survey from January to June 2024 among 1630 of 1800 invited first‐ and second‐year students at 9 medical colleges in Islamabad (response rate, 90.6%). Symptoms were assessed with the Patient Health Questionnaire‐9 (PHQ‐9) and Generalized Anxiety Disorder‐7 (GAD‐7).

title: Cutaneous Mast Cell Tumor With Metastasis in a Pet Cairo Spiny Mouse (Acomys cahirinus): A Case Report With Clinicopathologic Characterization
creator: Stephanie E Anderson, Amanda Smith, Shanna R Nelson, Keiichi Kuroki, Chidozie Egbu
description: A 3‐year‐old male pet Cario spiny mouse (Acomys cahirinus) presented with an exophytic, sessile dermal mass at the base of the left ear. Histopathological examination of the excisional biopsy revealed a poorly demarcated, densely cellular neoplasm composed of sheets of round to polygonal cells containing variably distinct basophilic to amphophilic fine intracytoplasmic granules.

title: Metastasis of Pancreatic Intraductal Oncocytic Papillary Neoplasm to the Ovaries
creator: Emily Fronk, Jamie McDowell, Natalia Yanchenko, Hani Katerji, Ashlee Smith, Marcel C C Machado
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesIntraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasm (IOPN) is a digestive system tumor typically found in the head of the pancreas. Most often, they remain confined to the pancreas; it is rare that they develop into an invasive carcinoma or metastasize.MethodsThis paper presents the case of a 63‐year‐old postmenopausal female with a past medical history notable for BRCA1 mutation and exploratory laparotomy with pancreatoduodenectomy who underwent risk‐reducing laparoscopic bilateral salpingo‐oophorectomy.ResultsPostoperative pathology revealed metastatic oncocytic papillary neoplasm involving the bilateral ovaries.

title: XIST Is a Key Modulator Associated With the Adhesome Network
creator: Dongning Chen, Nolan Origer, Sha Sun, Timothy L. Downing
description: A long non‐coding RNA (lncRNA) known as the X‐inactivation specific transcript (XIST) plays a central role in X chromosome inactivation—a transcriptional process that silences one of the two X chromosomes in females to ensure dosage compensation between males and females.

title: Real-world use of bempedoic acid for hypercholesterolaemia: a German multicentre, retrospective, cohort study
creator: Linus Haberbosch, Andrea Baessler, Ulrike de Ruiter, David Sinning, Julius L Katzmann, Stephanie Könemann, Ulrike Schatz, Knut Mai, Ursula Kassner, Thomas Bobbert
description: BackgroundDyslipidaemia remains a leading cause of death in Germany despite an improving therapeutic landscape, with many patients not achieving guideline-recommended low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) goals. Bempedoic acid, an adenosine triphosphate citrate lyase inhibitor, is a recent addition to the therapeutic landscape with proven efficacy in randomised controlled trials; however, its use varies between centres.

title: Structural characteristics of local cortical networks wired by distance dependent connectivity rules
creator: Bernhard Hellwig
description: BackgroundThe function of the cerebral cortex is shaped by its anatomical connectivity, yet experimental findings on connection probabilities in local cortical networks remain inconsistent. This study explores structural characteristics of local cortical networks based on distance dependent, Gaussian connectivity profiles. Monolayers of 101 × 101 pyramidal neurons were examined. Their connectivity was based on experimental anatomical or electrophysiological data.

title: Beyond ER-Golgi trafficking: unconventional protein secretion as a new design frontier for synthetic secretion switches in mammalian cells
creator: Bingshun Shi, Xinyuan Qiu, Yongheng Jiang, Jiabo Cai, Lingyun Zhu
description: Mammalian gene switches enable programmable cell behavior. However, current switches on transcriptional and translational layers require de novo RNA and protein synthesis, and secreted outputs must additionally undergo folding, post-translational processing, and intracellular trafficking, imposing delays that limit rapid extracellular responses. Rapid secretion-control switches instead act on pre-synthesized proteins by controlling retention, trafficking, storage, or release.

title: Are we back to normal? Evaluating the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on referrals to a child protection service in a tertiary care centre in Vienna, Austria
creator: Chryssa Grylli, Sophie Klomfar, Johanna Brandlechner, Laura Schaller, Katharina Weimann, Anastasia Pantazidou, Eva Mora-Theuer, Christoph Krall, Catherine Quantin, Susanne Greber-Platzer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundReports worldwide on suspected child maltreatment (CM) during and after the COVID-19 pandemic have been inconsistent. As no study has yet systematically examined whether structural disruptions to child protection systems have left measurable and lasting traces in referral patterns beyond the acute crisis phase, this study investigated the pandemic’s impact on suspected CM referrals to the Forensic Examination Center for Children and Adolescents (FOKUS) in Vienna, Austria, and whether enduring shifts in CM presentation and referral dynamics have occurred.MethodsRetrospective study using patient

title: Campylobacter jejuni as a Rare Pathogen in CIED Pocket Infections: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Karolina Barańska-Pawełczak, Bettina Ziaja, Mariusz Opara, Wojciech Jacheć
description: Patient: Male, 74-year-old Final Diagnosis Campylobacter jejuni infection Symptoms: Swelling of the pacemaker pocket Clinical Procedure: — Specialty: Cardiology Objective: Rare disease BackgroundCardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) infections are usually caused by gram-positive bacteria, whereas gram-negative pathogens are uncommon.Case ReportWe report a case of pacemaker pocket infection caused by Campylobacter jejuni in an immunocompromised patient.

title: Ancestral Sequences Cannot be Accurately Reconstructed via Interpolation in a Variational Autoencoder’s Latent Space
creator: Evan Gorstein, Mengze Tang, Hailey Bruzzone, Claudia Solís-Lemus
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Standard methods for ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) rely on substitution models for the residues in a biological sequence and assume independent evolution across these sites, ignoring the epistatic interactions that shape molecular evolution. In contrast, deep learning models like variational autoencoders (VAEs) can learn low-dimensional representations (“embeddings") of sequences in a protein family that may implicitly handle these dependencies, raising the possibility of performing more accurate ASR by interpolating between extant sequence embeddings within the VAE’s latent space.

title: TAPESTRY study: impact of prior transurethral resection of the prostate on outcomes after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a propensity score-matched cohort study
creator: Sebastian Lenart, Julia Zach, Georg Gutjahr, Lukas Oberhammer, Stephan Madersbacher, Anton Ponholzer, Clemens Mikulits, Andreas Banner
description: Prior transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) may distort bladder neck and apical anatomy and complicate robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP). Its effect on anastomotic recovery and oncological control remains controversial. To evaluate perioperative, anastomotic, pathological, and available PSA outcomes after RARP in patients with and without prior TURP.

title: Integrating optimal patient-centered care: patient- and family-reported experiences after complex treatment for rare diseases
creator: Frederiek L. Tijssens, Philippine Kies, Lissy de Ridder, Anne P. J. de Pagter, Jeanine M. M. van Klink
description: BackgroundAlthough life expectancy after complex treatments for rare diseases during childhood has increased, long-term medical, psychosocial and societal impacts remain for children and their families. Evaluating patient and family experiences is essential for the development and optimization of integrated patient-centered, value-based care pathways.

title: Tangier Disease
creator: Sabitha Sasidharan Pillai, Preneet Cheema Brar, Ambika P Ashraf
description: Purpose of ReviewWe describe two patients with Tangier disease (TD) and provide a narrative review of its clinical features, genetics, diagnosis, and management. A literature search of PubMed and Google Scholar was performed to identify English-language publications on TD, and relevant articles were reviewed narratively.

title: Central gland detachment following prostate artery embolization: incidence, risk factors and clinical outcomes
creator: Fergus O’Herlihy, Sean Collins, Matthew Laffey, Kiaran O’Malley, Richard E. Power, Cormac Farrelly
description: BackgroundCentral gland detachment (CGD) is a potential complication following prostate artery embolisation (PAE). There is limited information regarding its incidence, associated risk factors, and voiding and ejaculatory function after CGD.MethodsSixty-five consecutive patients undergoing PAE in a single institution were included in this retrospective cohort study. Baseline demographics, radiologic, procedural and clinical outcome data were gathered for all patients.

title: An Exploratory Accounting Approach for Balancing Environmental Impacts of Point and Diffuse Sources in Nitrogen Trading
creator: Jing Lu, Katherine R. O’Brien, Felix Egger, Tony Weber, Jon M. Olley, Matthew P. Adams, Michele A. Burford
description: Nutrient trading between point and diffuse sources of nutrients offers an integrated watershed nutrient management approach to achieve nutrient reduction goals that benefit both the terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems. This market-based approach requires quantification of the environmental impacts of nutrients derived from different sources. This environmental impact depends on the forms, concentrations, loads, transport, and processing of nutrients within waterways.

title: Explaining symptoms in general practice: a predictive processing framework for primary care consultations
creator: Kees van Boven, Peter Lucassen, Tim Olde Hartman, Omer Van den Bergh
description: AimsTo present predictive processing as a clinically useful framework for explaining symptom variability in general practice consultations.MethodsDevelopment of a conceptual framework through an iterative process of theoretical synthesis and clinical translation, informed by a supporting literature search integrating literature on predictive processing and symptom perception with primary care literature on consultation practice and persistent physical symptoms.

title: How does a national blood operator detect early infectious disease signals affecting blood and cellular therapy product safety and sufficiency?
creator: Leisa Bruneau, Carmen L Charlton, Sandra Ramirez‐Arcos, Dilini Kumaran, David Allan, Olivia Norman, Matthew Seftel, Evan M Bloch, Chantale Pambrun, Sheila F O'Brien, Cynthia Cranney, Steven J Drews
description: BackgroundPublic access to up‐to‐date information on infectious diseases and outbreaks has grown rapidly with the advent of artificial intelligence platforms. While this information can improve patient care and support research, the sheer volume of available data coupled with the challenge of identifying misinformation and disinformation can be overwhelming.

title: Fungal extracellular vesicles reshape Lactobacillus rhamnosus vesicles to enhance lysosomal homeostasis and resolve intestinal inflammation
creator: Zhengmei Ji, Guoliang Chen, Xiaolong He, Xiangqian Zhang, Bin Chen, Hang Xiao, Yurong Guo, Yanhui Han
description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are emerging mediators of intercellular and interkingdom communication. While bacterial EVs directly modulate host health, whether exogenous vesicles can reprogram gut microbial vesiculation and bioactivity remains unclear. Using a defined in vitro conditioning system, ScEV exposure altered EV production by Lactobacillus rhamnosus, generating ScEV-conditioned L. rhamnosus vesicles (ScEV-LrEVs).

title: Impact of Concomitant Grade I Degenerative Spondylolisthesis on Clinical and Radiographic Outcomes
creator: Hinpetch Daungsupawong, Viroj Wiwanitkit
description: ficant issue, as degenerative spondylolisthesis grade I often complicates the decision-making process for decompression in patients with lumbar spinal stenosis. Analysis found that the presence of DS1 did not significantly alter 12-month clinical outcomes between biportal endoscopic laminectomy and microscopic laminectomy.

title: Cognitive Function Influences Longitudinal Motor Function Recovery after Proximal Femoral Fracture: A Longitudinal Analysis
creator: Takehiro Kaneoka, Tomohiro Kawazoe, Kazuhiro Yamazaki, Gen Shiraishi, Takashi Sakai
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Objectives:As the incidence of proximal femoral fractures (PFFs) continues to increase, optimizing patient-specific treatment strategies is essential for the efficient use of healthcare resources. The aim of this study was to examine longitudinal postoperative motor function recovery in patients with femoral neck fractures (FNF) and intertrochanteric fractures (ITFs) and to identify which factors, including fracture type and patient-related characteristics, predominantly influence recovery trajectories to inform individualized rehabilitation strategies.Methods:This retrospective study included patients who underwent bipolar hip arthroplasty for FNF (201 hips) or

title: Your voice matters: using participatory film to engage people with chronic pain in public involvement and research
creator: Sarah A. Harrisson, Samina Begum, Claire Toussaint, Mark Agathangelou, James Rattee, Melanie A. Holden, Krysia Canvin
description: BackgroundPeople living with chronic pain (≥ 3-months) often struggle to participate in valued activity (for example, family life, work and in their community) and are under-represented in public involvement and research. We aimed to broaden awareness and encourage engagement in public involvement and research among people living with chronic pain.

title: Standardizing Rectal Suction Biopsy Preparation With a Dedicated Equipment Box: A Quality Improvement Project
creator: Yasir Alkhatib
description: Rectal suction biopsy is an established diagnostic procedure for suspected Hirschsprung disease, but reliable performance depends on having multiple pieces of equipment, consumables, specimen containers, and documentation immediately available. In our paediatric surgical clinical area, the required items were stored in different locations, resulting in avoidable searching, workflow interruptions, and the possibility of missing essential equipment during preparation.

title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Following Two-Tined Three-Site Conventional Radiofrequency Ablation of Genicular Nerves for Chronic Knee Pain
creator: Mingda Chen, Sercan Tosun, Nicolas R Thompson, Kush Goyal
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation (GNRFA) has emerged as an effective therapy for chronic knee pain. Although some studies have evaluated its effectiveness, there is limited real-world data on the long-term patient-reported outcome (PRO) data for GNRFAs.Objective: This study aimed to evaluate PROs following conventional GNRFAs performed using two-tined electrodes and the classical three-site technique targeting the superior medial, superior lateral, and inferior medial genicular nerves.Methods: We performed a retrospective chart review to gather data from consecutive GNRFAs at an academic medical

title: Imaging nanoscopic co-assemblies of α-synuclein and Tau in human samples
creator: Yu P Zhang, Amber Wallis, Clara Obensa Bertroli, Cherida Zhang, Melanie Burke, Florence Layburn, Evgeniia Lobanova, Martin Furlepa, Shekhar Kedia, Yuhao Cui, Prasanna Suresh, Woo Suk Yang, Annelies Quaegebeur, Tim Bartels, Caroline H Williams-Gray, David Klenerman
description: α-synuclein (αS), amyloid-β (Aβ), and Tau aggregates are hallmarks of many neurodegenerative diseases, yet the prevalence and nature of their nanoscopic co-assemblies remain poorly understood. Here, we adapt a single-molecule pull-down (SiMPull) assay to profile αS, Aβ, and Tau co-assemblies across post-mortem brain tissue homogenates, soluble brain fractions, human serum, cerebrospinal fluid, and saliva.

title: Comparability of food frequency questionnaires between Korean Children’s Environmental Health Study (Ko-CHENS) and Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES) in pregnant women
creator: Minsu Cho, Bom Kim, Hyesook Kim, Sunghun Na, Se Jin Lee, Tae Gyu Ahn, Kyung Ho Son, Woo Jin Kim, Jung Eun Lee, Ko-CHENS Study Group
description: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVESThe Korean Children’s Environmental Health Study (Ko-CHENS) developed a food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) to assess maternal dietary intake during pregnancy. This FFQ shares high structural similarity with the validated FFQ of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES), a representative dietary assessment tool for the Korean adult population, which includes 97 of the 112 items in the Ko-CHENS FFQ.

title: Structural alterations in the superior temporal gyrus associated with depressive symptoms in migraine without aura: a voxel-based morphometry and surface-based morphometry magnetic resonance imaging study
creator: Donghai Chen, Yayin Luo, Yuhao Zhang, Wenlong Zhang, Zhuqing Yuan, Zhixuan He, Haochong Xie, Meijun Qu, Tong Lin, Jiawei Li, Qingwei Song, Yanwei Miao, Zhe Wang, Jian Jiang, Renwang Pu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMigraine without aura (MwoA) frequently co-occurs with depressive symptoms, yet the neurobiological mechanisms underlying this comorbidity remain insufficiently characterized. This study integrated voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and surface-based morphometry (SBM) to compare gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical morphology between patients with MwoA and healthy controls (HC) and to further determine whether structural brain alterations vary across MwoA subgroups stratified by depressive symptom severity, thereby identifying potential structural correlates of depressive symptoms in this population.MethodsA total of 67 patients with MwoA {38 with

title: Genetic diversity and morphology of South Korean Aedes koreicus (Diptera: Culicidae) provide insights into the origin of European populations
creator: Junyoung Lee, Jungyoon Lee, Changseob Lim, Ji Hyoun Kang, Sangwoo Seok, Hee Il Lee, Yeon Jae Bae
description: BackgroundAedes koreicus (Edwards, 1917) is native to Korea, northern China, and the Russian Far East, and has gained attention following its first detection in Europe in 2008 and subsequent spread across Europe. The Korean Peninsula, which includes the type locality of Ae.

title: Low-dose, high-frequency simulation with respiratory function monitor feedback enhances face mask ventilation across neonatal resuscitation devices: A prospective study in neonatology fellows
creator: Samantha J Carlton, Joseph L Hagan, Nicole K Neveln, Daniel S Lemke, Nathan C Sundgren
description: Face mask ventilation (FMV) is a critical skill in neonatal resuscitation, yet structured assessment of neonatology fellow competence has remained limited. This study evaluated whether low-dose, high-frequency simulation with real-time respiratory function monitor (RFM) feedback improved FMV performance across commonly used ventilation devices.

title: A telomere-to-telomere assembly of the white mulberry (Morus alba) genome provides insights into karyotype evolution and the white-fruit phenotype in Morus
creator: Fangfang Peng, Xunlan Li, Zhaoxin Wei, Guohui Han, Xiaoyu Wang
description: r n = 14 [2]. To date, telomere-to-telomere (T2T) genomes have been reported for the wild species Morus notabilis (n = 7) [3] and Morus mongolica (n = 14) [4]. However, white mulberry (M. alba), the most widely cultivated species within the n = 14 group, lacks a complete T2T reference genome. Such a resource would address two major limitations.

title: TrenibotulinumtoxinE: Pharmacology, clinical evidence, and emerging role in aesthetic medicine
creator: Chaocheng Liu, Jean Carruthers, Alain Michon
description: SummaryBotulinum neurotoxin type A (BoNT/A) products are among the most popular aesthetic treatments worldwide, but their relatively prolonged duration may be a barrier for patients who are concerned about unnatural appearance, adverse effects, or being committed to an unwanted result.

title: Prescribing for the patient and the planet: a pragmatic feasibility study of a behaviour change intervention to reduce liquid amoxicillin prescribing in primary care
creator: Adam Pattison Rathbone, Joseph Pickles, Ms Laura Griffiths, Alice McCloskey, Philippa McCabe, Nicola Vasey, Emma Lim
description: BackgroundOral liquid medicines can be clinically appropriate but may be used when solid oral formulations are feasible, with implications for medicine costs and environmental sustainability. We evaluated the feasibility of GPILL, a theory-informed intervention using prescribing feedback, social norms and information on formulation-associated carbon dioxide equivalent (CO₂e) emissions to support reduced liquid amoxicillin prescribing in primary care.

title: A systematic review of intracranial atherosclerosis epidemiology—the largest contributor to the global ischemic stroke burden?
creator: Davor Pavlin-Premrl, Vincent Thijs, Peter J. Mitchell, Nawaf Yassi, Mark Parsons, Anna H. Balabanski, Julian Maingard, Hamed Asadi, Ashu Jhamb, Ali Khabaza, Adam Zheng, Aaron Gaekwad, Catherine Voutier, Bruce CV. Campbell
description: BackgroundIntracranial atherosclerosis (ICAD) is commonly stated to be the largest contributor to the ischemic stroke burden worldwide. However, there has been little systematic examination of the epidemiology literature.MethodsPubMed, OVID-EMBASE and manual searches of references from retrieved literature were used to identify studies. Adult studies from 1990 onwards were included, with two reviewers independently reviewing titles and abstracts.

title: Exploring the effects of digital literacy training on college students’ self-leadership: a longitudinal randomized controlled trial
creator: Kefei Tan
description: ObjectiveSelf-leadership is recognized as a critical self-regulatory capacity for academic success and personal development. While prior correlational studies have linked digital literacy to self-regulated learning, experimental evidence for a potential directional pathway from digital literacy enhancement to self-leadership development remains scarce.

title: Primary cutaneous adenoid cystic carcinoma arising in the axilla: a case report and literature review
creator: Si Li, Fang Yang, Yangyang Jiang, Shuanghai Hu
description: Primary cutaneous adenoid cystic carcinoma (PCACC) is a rare cutaneous adnexal malignancy. Although its clinical course is generally considered more indolent than that of salivary gland-derived counterparts, PCACC exhibits a significant propensity for local recurrence and a notable potential for distant metastasis. Here, we report a rare case of PCACC arising in the right axilla.

title: Spatial multi-omics-guided drug development in inflammatory bowel disease: from mucosal immune niches to precision therapy
creator: Hai Wang, Xiaolong Zhao, Jie Yang
description: Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis are now treated with an expanding set of biologics and small molecules, yet treatment selection remains largely empirical. Primary non-response, secondary loss of response, incomplete mucosal healing, fibrostenosis, and fistulizing disease show that conventional clinical, endoscopic, and bulk molecular markers do not capture how disease is organized within tissue.

title: Early time-of-day infusion of PD-1 inhibitor improves prognosis in advanced gastric cancer: a multicenter real-world study
creator: Ziting Qu, Xiaoyu Guo, Shupei Zhang, Yanyan Zhao, Zhenyan Hu, Wenxi Ding, Sachiyo Nomura, Yiyin Zhang, Xiaoli Wei
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundWhether the time-of-day administration (ToDA) of programmed cell death 1 (PD-1) inhibitor infusion influences survival in advanced gastric cancer (AGC) remains unclear. This research aimed to evaluate the impact of ToDA on the prognosis of AGC patients.MethodsThis multicenter retrospective study enrolled 416 AGC patients receiving PD-1 inhibitor therapy, who were divided into early and late ToDA groups based on sensitivity analyses using 30-minute intervals of the administration time window.

title: Editorial: Case reports in veterinary neurology and neurosurgery, volume II
creator: Koen M. Santifort, Joao Miguel De Frias, Simone Spinillo, Bruno A. Lopes, Susana Monforte Monteiro
description: nge of subjects, including clinical phenomena, histopathological diagnoses, genetic disorders, and other. In this second volume (Case Reports in Veterinary Neurology and Neurosurgery, Volume II), no less than 24 articles are included. Of these, nine pertain to cats, one to foxes, and 14 to dogs.

title: Ozoralizumab, a trivalent anti-TNFα NANOBODY® compound, is resistant to rheumatoid factor-mediated modulation of FcRn-dependent recycling and immune complex uptake
creator: Mai Morimoto, Yukihisa Sawa, Chihiro Ishiwatari-Ogata, Naoki Kojima, Yasuyuki Fujii
description: Rheumatoid factor (RF), an autoantibody targeting IgG, is a key diagnostic marker of autoimmune diseases, especially rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In patients with RA, high RF titers have been reported to be associated with disease severity and may influence the pharmacological behavior and clinical response of certain biologic agents, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors.

title: Sepsis-associated thrombotic microangiopathy–like syndrome following cardiac surgery: a case report
creator: Chujun Yang, Shanshan Dong, Zhijing Xia, Wan Peng, Hua Yan, Zhenlu Zhang, Qimei Wei
description: Severe sepsis following cardiac surgery may be accompanied by a thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA)-like syndrome distinct from classic immune-mediated thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) and overt disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). We report a 62-year-old man who developed sepsis after mitral valve replacement, complicated by thrombocytopenia (nadir 45 × 10⁹/L), microangiopathic hemolysis (2.6% schistocytes), and multiple organ dysfunction.

title: Role of the ketogenic diet in neurodevelopmental disorders: neuroprotection and clinical practice
creator: Luqiang Sun, Liu Qu, Shuqing Gao, Juan Chen, Pan Wu, Haichuan Wang
description: Neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), occur early in life and affect cognitive and behavioral health and motor development. While hereditary factors contribute to the development of ASD, recent research has shown that environmental factors, notably nutritional factors, play important roles in determining the severity and expression of symptoms.

title: Onco-anxiology: a proposal for an anxiety-focused, longitudinal framework within cancer care
creator: Chirag Jain
description: BackgroundAnxiety is among the most common forms of psychological distress in people with cancer, yet in routine practice it is usually addressed within a broad “distress” construct rather than as a distinct clinical target.ObjectiveThis Perspective examines whether anxiety warrants a dedicated, longitudinally organised clinical focus, and proposes onco-anxiology as such a framework within psycho-oncology.

title: Mapping the genomic landscape of two key human gut microbial species: Bifidobacterium infantis and Bifidobacterium longum
creator: Marco Ventura
description: late into functional variation that shapes microbial ecology, host interactions, and ultimately host health, thereby enabling a more rational and predictive approach to designing health-promoting microorganisms. A key biological insight from this work[1] is the extensive genomic heterogeneity within both B. longum subsp. infantis and B. longum subsp.

title: Efgartigimod combined with rituximab helps improve the symptoms and reduce the use of corticosteroids in patients with MuSK antibody-positive MG: a single case report
creator: Xiujun Zheng, Jing Wang, Tongtong Cai, Houshi Zhou
description: IntroductionMyasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder primarily affecting the neuromuscular junction. Muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase antibody (MuSK-Ab)-mediated MG often presents with bulbar weakness and is prone to crisis. Currently, conventional treatments show limited efficacy in MuSK-Ab-mediated MG, while rituximab therapy demonstrates favorable outcomes.

title: Intersecting epidemics: deciphering the complexities of tuberculosis-diabetes comorbidity
creator: Mariana Araujo-Pereira, Caian L. Vinhaes, Beatriz Barreto-Duarte, Klauss Villalva-Serra, Artur T. L. Queiroz, Bruno B. Andrade
description: Within the global health landscape, tuberculosis (TB) presents an ongoing challenge, demanding innovative strategies for its control. This review spotlights the intersection of TB with diabetes mellitus (DM), recognized by the World Health Organization as a key risk factor in the TB epidemic.

title: Updated chorology, habitat ecology, conservation assessment and habitat suitability of Centaurea jankae in Romania and Bulgaria
creator: Simona Dumitriţa Chirilă, Nicu Alexandru Gîlea, Mihai Doroftei, Stoyan Nikolov, Kiril Vassilev
description: Centaurea jankae is a rare species with a restricted distribution in southeastern Romania and northeastern Bulgaria. This study aimed to update the chorology of C. jankae, characterise its habitat ecology and population-level variation, assess its local conservation condition, and model its current potential distribution and habitat suitability.

title: The clinical landscape of bladder cancer treatment: a brief report on new developments and future perspectives in pharmaceutical interventions
creator: Xiao Xu, Hai-Yan Hao, Hai-Yan Chen
description: This study systematically delineates the clinical research status and trends in bladder cancer (Bca) therapeutics through an analysis of 1024 Bca drug treatment clinical trials identified from a harmonised search of the Trialtrove database, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP) database as of December 31, 2025.

title: A rare case of gastroenteritis due to salmonella enterica serovar Infantis in South India
creator: S. C. Shruthi Shree, Yogeesh D. Maheshwarappa, Mahadevaiah Neelambike Sumana, Deepashree Rajshekar, Supreeta R. Shettar, G. K. Megha, Veerabhadraswamy G. S., Chinchana Shylaja Eshwarappa, Morubagal Raghavendra Rao, Vidhyavathi B. Chitharagi
description: Salmonella enterica serovar Infantis is an emerging non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) serovar increasingly associated with foodborne gastroenteritis. Human infections caused by this serovar remain underreported in India. We report a case of acute gastroenteritis caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Infantis in a 53-year-old male from South India.

title: Editorial: Exploring neuropsychiatric disorders through multimodal MRI: network analysis, biomarker discovery, and clinical insights
creator: Ruichen Ren, Wei Wang
description: e microstructure, functional activity, and dynamic network organization, thereby providing a multidimensional characterization of disease-related brain alterations. In highly heterogeneous brain disorders, similar clinical manifestations do not necessarily arise from the same biological substrates, and subtle alterations in brain networks may emerge before clinically apparent functional impairment.

title: Correlation analysis between tongue hyperspectral imaging and tongue coating microbiota and feasibility study for early screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus status
creator: Zhao-wei Liu, Yan Zhang, Lei Fu, Jing-ya Xie, Xin-yu Zhang, Ming Liu, Jing Zhao
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the feasibility of applying hyperspectral imaging technology combined with machine learning algorithms for early non-invasive screening of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).MethodsIn this study, tongue images of 153 subjects were acquired using a hyperspectral imaging system. Concurrently, 53 tongue coating samples were collected for 16S rRNA sequencing.

title: From reference epigenomes to response epigenomes: a public-health case built on the developing brain
creator: Thomas Hartung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Reference epigenome projects, such as the NIH roadmap, ENCODE, and the international human epigenome consortium, have started mapping the baseline regulatory states of human cell types with extraordinary detail. However, these projects were not designed to address the urgent questions posed by exposome science and child-health policy: how these states change after environmental exposure, in whom, during which developmental window, and whether they can recover.

title: Efficacy and safety of pulsed radiofrequency combined with nerve block for cervical radiculopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Xiaogang Hao, Xinxin Tian, Fengling Sun, Qi An, Jiajun Zhao, Yueliang Sun, Guohui Zhou, Mingpeng Shi, Xinhua Chen
description: BackgroundCervical radiculopathy is a common cause of neck–shoulder–arm pain and functional impairment. Although nerve block provides rapid analgesia, its durability may be limited. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether pulsed radiofrequency combined with nerve block offers superior efficacy and comparable safety to nerve block alone.MethodsEight databases were searched from inception to April 10, 2026.

title: Interpretable admission-stage machine learning for early Sepsis-3 identification in the emergency department
creator: Fulden Cantaş Türkiş, Buğra Varol
description: Background/objectivesArtificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems have emerged as promising tools for improving early sepsis recognition in emergency departments. This study aimed to develop and evaluate interpretable machine learning models for identifying Sepsis-3-defined sepsis using routinely available admission-stage variables and to compare their performance with conventional biomarkers and the Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS).

title: Sport specialization predicts athletic identity exclusivity in youth athletes: a three-wave RI-CLPM study of controlling coaching and non-sport peer restriction with implications for adolescent care
creator: Xishan Liu, Hao Liu, Feng Shao, Dongdong Ma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSport specialization has usually been examined through biomedical outcomes such as overuse injury, burnout, and premature dropout. Less is known about whether specialization is prospectively associated with adolescent identity development by narrowing opportunities for exploration beyond sport.

title: Effects of dietary fucoidan and exercise on the gut microbiome, fecal metabolome, and tumor-related responses in a murine colorectal cancer model
creator: Lin Zhong, Bhagyalakshmi Purushothaman, Xingxiang Wang, Yucheng Zhang, Xiangze Sun, Jiyi Jiang, Karamveer Karamveer, Youming Zhang, Qiang Tu, Boopathi Seenivasan
description: Dietary fucoidan, a sulfated polysaccharide derived from brown seaweed, has attracted increasing interest for its potential to influence gut microbial and metabolic responses. However, the individual and combined effects of dietary fucoidan and exercise on host–microbiome interactions during colorectal cancer development remain incompletely understood.

title: Disease-specific patterns of glymphatic-related dysfunction between multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
creator: Xiaoya Chen, Kai Zhang, Xiaojuan Dong, Xiaohui Zhang, Zhuowei Shi, Zichun Yan, Qiyuan Zhu, Yuling Peng, Yongliang Han, Yongmei Li
description: BackgroundGlymphatic dysfunction has been reported in multiple sclerosis (MS) and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), yet disease-specific patterns of glymphatic-related impairment and their structural and cognitive consequences remain poorly characterized.MethodsThis study enrolled 196 MS patients, 88 NMOSD patients, and 108 healthy controls (HC).

title: Timing of nebulized colistimethate sodium following bronchodilator airway conditioning in hospital-acquired pneumonia: a target trial emulation study
creator: Yi Cui, Qiannan Zhao, Jianning Zhang, Siyu Lu, Shuai Li, Lufeng Zhao, Ming Gao, Hao Chen, Hui Han, Xiaofang Huang
description: BackgroundEvidence for nebulized colistimethate sodium (CMS) in hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) remains inconsistent, potentially due to heterogeneity in airway conditions and delivery timing. We evaluated whether timely initiation of nebulized CMS following bronchodilator airway pre-treatment was associated with microbiological outcomes in critically ill patients.

title: Fit one model, report one number: how to analyse a training or intervention study
creator: Gudrun Schappacher-Tilp, Markus Tilp
description: A typical training or intervention study allocates participants to protocols, measures them repeatedly over time, and asks whether one protocol changes the outcome more than another. A typical analysis, such as an analysis of variance or a mixed model, is powerful, but that power is for taking a measurement apart, not for delivering the verdict.

title: A machine learning model for predicting six-month rehospitalization in heart failure patients with multiple comorbidities
creator: Rahul Awasthy, Michael L. Seavers, Aayush Awasthy
description: This research (retrospective cohort study) investigates how tailored discharge instructions for heart failure (HF) patients with multiple health conditions can lower their emergency or urgent care readmission risk. Utilizing an AI/ML approach, this study develops a model that classifies HF patients' readmission risk at discharge by evaluating approximately 20 parameters across five categories, including comorbidities (e.g.

title: Wearable biosensors characterize Baguazhang exercise intensity, trunk acceleration, and cardiovascular autonomic adaptations in postmenopausal women
creator: Jinjin Cao, Meijuan Zhang
description: BackgroundBaguazhang is a traditional Chinese mind-body exercise that combines circular locomotion, repeated changes of direction, lower-limb postural control, trunk rotation, coordinated upper-limb movements, and breathing regulation. These features make it a multicomponent movement practice, but its cardiovascular intensity and trunk-acceleration profile have not been well quantified in postmenopausal women.

title: The predictive value of aGAPSS score combined with clinical factors for thrombosis in systemic lupus erythematosus
creator: Juan Shi, Libo Ouyang, Qiong Ma, Peiming Zheng
description: PurposeThis study evaluated the predictive value of antiphospholipid antibodies (aPLs) combined with the adjusted global antiphospholipid syndrome score (aGAPSS) for thrombosis in hospitalized systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) patients.MethodsA retrospective analysis included 309 SLE patients (65 with in-hospital thrombosis, 244 without). Demographic, clinical, and serological data were collected.

title: From environmental awareness to ecological behavior: a bibliometric mapping of the literature
creator: Fikret Kayhalak, Suat Karaküçük
description: This study maps the intellectual, conceptual, and social structure of the research literature connecting environmental awareness to ecological behavior through a systematic bibliometric analysis. Bibliographic records were retrieved from Web of Science (WoS) Core Collection and Scopus using a comprehensive dual-database search strategy, yielding 934 unique publications after duplicate removal. A database complementarity analysis revealed that 222 records (23.

title: When metagenomic next-generation sequencing detects Nocardia: from clinical interpretation to immune-based clinical management
creator: Ping Li, Xiao Yang, Yuxia Chen, Lili Wang, Qiqi Cui, Zhihong Wu, Fenglin Cao
description: BackgroundMetagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) increasingly detects Nocardia, but interpreting positive results remains challenging. We aimed to identify host factors and read thresholds that distinguish nocardiosis (ND) from colonization/contamination, and to characterize clinical features linked to immune status.MethodsA retrospective analysis from 74 patients at Qilu Hospital of Shandong University from April 2022 to October 2025 was conducted.

title: Glycemic burden-adjusted urinary glucose excretion deficit is associated with hyperuricemia in patients with type 2 diabetes
creator: Liying Wang, Yun Wang, Ying Gong, Houfa Geng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo investigate the associations of glycemic burden-adjusted urinary glucose excretion deficit (GB-UGE deficit) with serum uric acid levels and prevalent hyperuricemia in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).MethodsA total of 887 patients with T2DM were enrolled. GB-UGE deficit was defined as the inverse standardized residual from a linear regression of ln(urinary glucose excretion + 1) on glycated hemoglobin, fasting glucose, 2-hour postprandial glucose and eGFR; a higher GB-UGE deficit indicates less urinary glucose excretion than expected for a given glycemic burden.

title: A predictive model of serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D for recurrence of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo in the elderly: a single-center follow-up cohort study
creator: Xue Zhang, Xizuo Pu, Yingmei Wang, Xingya Li, Qingchun Pan
description: ObjectivesTo investigate the predictive value of serum calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25-OH-VD) on recurrence after canalith repositioning procedure (CRP) in elderly patients with benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV), and to establish a quantitative prediction model.MethodsA single-center follow-up cohort study was conducted involving 286 elderly BPPV patients (age≥60 years) treated with CRP from January 2020 to June 2025.

title: Temporal and clinical heterogeneity of double M-protein multiple myeloma: diagnostic and treatment-emergent phenotypes
creator: Dangui Chen, Fusheng Yao
description: BackgroundDouble M-protein multiple myeloma (DMP-MM) is an uncommon phenotype characterized by more than one detectable monoclonal component on serum protein electrophoresis and/or immunofixation electrophoresis. Its clinical significance is uncertain, particularly when a secondary component appears after therapy.MethodsWe retrospectively studied 21 patients with DMP-MM treated at Anqing Municipal Hospital.

title: Dissociation between humoral and multi-omic immune responses to inactivated COVID-19 vaccination in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis
creator: Zhijie Jiang, Pengfei Jin, Xiaorui Nie, Jin Wei, Siyue Jia, Qiao Liu, Mingwei Wei, Xiaoyan Ding, Daming Zhou, Liguo Zhu, Limei Zhu, Mulong Du, Jingxin Li
description: IntroductionPatients with pulmonary tuberculosis (PTB) may experience persistent immune dysregulation during anti-tuberculosis treatment, yet vaccine evaluation in this population has largely relied on humoral endpoints. Whether preserved antibody responses reflect coordinated systems-level immune activation after inactivated COVID-19 vaccination remains unclear. This study used systems vaccinology to identify multi-omic immune signatures induced by vaccination in PTB patients.

title: Effects of multicultural piano education on children's psychosocial wellbeing: the roles of cross-cultural musical competence and cultural identity
creator: Qi Yu, Panghua Tian
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionChildren's psychosocial wellbeing is closely linked to emotional regulation, social competence, self-esteem, resilience, and cultural identity. Traditional piano instruction commonly prioritizes technical skills and Western classical repertoire, leaving its psychological and cross-cultural potential underexplored.

title: Repeated plantar electrical stimulation is associated with altered lower-limb somatosensory processing in older adults: evidence from somatosensory evoked potentials
creator: Aoi Mase, Risa Tashiro, Kanoko Ito, Ryoji Kasanami, Ryota Sakurai, Chiaki Ohtaka, Manabu Shibasaki, Hiroki Nakata
description: IntroductionAge-related declines in lower-limb somatosensory function may contribute to impaired motor control and increased fall risk in older adults. Although plantar sensory stimulation has been reported to improve postural control, its effects on neural processing remain unclear. This study investigated whether repeated plantar electrical stimulation modifies lower-limb somatosensory processing in older adults using somatosensory evoked potentials (SEPs).

title: Resting-state frontal theta/beta ratio and psychological symptoms in college students: an EEG study
creator: Duo Mi, Yuanyuan Li, Yan Zhu, Zhaoxin Guo, Lun Zhao
description: BackgroundMental health problems are increasingly prevalent among college students and represent an important public health concern. Neurophysiological indicators derived from electroencephalography (EEG) may provide objective markers for identifying psychological vulnerability. The theta/beta ratio (TBR) has been widely associated with attentional regulation and cognitive control; however, its relationship with multidimensional psychological symptoms in non-clinical populations remains insufficiently understood.

title: Embedding research education and scholarly project development into a medical education curriculum: a transferable glocalized curriculum model
creator: Cordelle Lazare, Leslie S. Craig, Rashida Daisley, Carlene Radix, Rhonda McIntyre
description: Early experiential learning, including participation in research and community-engaged health promotion, fosters critical thinking, scholarly development, and socially responsive practice; however, these opportunities remain inconsistently integrated into pre-clinical curricula. Dense foundational science content, limited faculty mentorship capacity, and reliance on optional engagement contribute to inequitable access, with participation often limited to higher-achieving students.

title: Case Report: Multisystem response to dupilumab in a child with atopic dermatitis, asthma, eosinophilic esophagitis, and other gastrointestinal manifestations
creator: Hua-Jie Yan, Wei Dong, Yu-Nan Yang, Chun-Yun Zeng
description: BackgroundAtopic dermatitis (AD), asthma, and eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) may coexist because they share type 2 inflammatory pathways. Evidence for dupilumab in children with EoE and other gastrointestinal manifestations remains limited.Case presentationA 7-year-old girl had poorly controlled AD, recurrent asthma, EoE (>100 eosinophils/high-power field), and lower-density eosinophilic infiltration in gastric, ileal, and colonic biopsies.

title: Trustworthiness assessment as an inclusion criterion for systematic reviews—What is the impact on results?
creator: Jo Weeks, Anna Cuthbert, Zarko Alfirevic
description: BackgroundThere is increasing concern that a significant proportion of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) included in Cochrane reviews may not be trustworthy. Applying the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Trustworthiness Screening Tool (CPC‐TST) has already had a clinically important effect on several reviews published by the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group.

title: Cultural appropriateness, co-creation, and subjective vitality: a pre–post structural modeling study of immersive performances in rural Guangdong, China
creator: Yuqi Shang
description: BackgroundThis study examined short-term changes in social connectedness and subjective vitality following culturally adapted, co-created immersive performances, and explored baseline-adjusted associations among cultural appropriateness, co-creation engagement, social connectedness, and vitality.MethodsA single-group pre–post field study was conducted across four communities in Guangdong, China. Data from 786 matched participants were analyzed using paired-samples tests and structural equation modeling with bootstrap estimation.

title: Nonlinear association between body roundness index and depressive symptoms in women of reproductive age: The mediating role of systemic inflammation
creator: Li Zhang, Xianmei Ma, Gaoyan Shi, Yanhua Liu
description: BackgroundPrevious studies reported a linear association between Body Roundness Index (BRI) and depressive symptoms in general adults, but the relationship in women of reproductive age remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between Body Roundness Index (BRI) and depressive symptoms and to examine the statistical mediating role of inflammatory markers in this association.

title: A Bionic Peristaltic Process for Enhanced Powder Dispersion in Energetic High-Solid-Loading Slurries
creator: Tong Zhou, Narenchaogetu He, Song Nie, Jiangbao Zeng, Jinbin Zou, Jie Liu
description: This study introduces a paddle-less bionic peristaltic mixing process, inspired by intestinal biomechanics, for enhanced powder dispersion in energetic high-solid-loading slurries (80% solids). Periodic elastic conduit compression induces low-shear vortices, substantially reducing energy consumption compared with conventional mechanical stirring in solid propellant preparation.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance-derived left atrioventricular coupling index for predicting adverse cardiac outcomes in patients with ischemic cardiomyopathy
creator: Sedthasith Treewatchareekorn, Sittinop Titichoatrattana, Paisit Kosum, Yossatorn Buranasakulsatid, Chayachon Okonogi, Monravee Tumkosit, Yongkasem Vorasettakarnkij, Pairoj Chattranukulchai, Nonthikorn Theerasuwipakorn
description: AbstarctBackgroundRisk stratification in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) traditionally relies on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), which may not fully demonstrate the complex interplay between atrium and ventricle. The left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI) has emerged as a promising integrative marker. This study evaluated the prognostic value of cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived LACI in patients with ICM.

title: Combined pneumonia and glandular tularemia following a tick bite in an immunocompromised patient
creator: Theo Van Gucht, Presenna Suntharasarma, Alia Barthel, Mahsa Mohseni-Zadeh, Guillaume Gregorowicz, Olivier Augereau, Victor Gerber, Martin Martinot
description: Francisella tularensis can cause a broad spectrum of clinical manifestations depending on the route of inoculation. In northeastern France, tick bites are a frequent route of transmission. Typically, vector-borne inoculation results in glandular or ulceroglandular forms, whereas aerosol exposure causes pulmonary forms.

title: LPS stimulation reveals male and female dimorphism in human iPSC-derived macrophages
creator: Pamela L. Graney, Daniel Naveed Tavakol, Roberta I. Lock, Connie Chen, Maria Samaritano, Eloy Sanchez, Nicole P. Hachmann, Montserrat Pineda Rosales, Richard Friedman, Gordana Vunjak-Novakovic
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryClinical disparities in the inflammatory responses between males and females have been reported for decades, revealing sex-biased disease severity and patient outcomes. To better understand the intrinsic biological sex differences contributing to these disparities, we characterized the functional and transcriptomic responses of induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived macrophages from male and female donors under control and inflammatory conditions using the bacterial antigen lipopolysaccharide (LPS).

title: A systematic transcriptomic atlas and predictive framework for metabolite-driven T cell state transitions
creator: Yiyang Xu, Yiheng Zhao, Sizhe Yang, Huimin Li, Xiangrong Diao, Qianqian Zhang, Shuting Yu, Shuai Wang, Fangying Jiang, Qiang Wang, Yuhua Ma, Bo Jiao, Yun Tan, Yabin Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryGut microbial and endogenous metabolites are key regulators at the interface of host metabolism and immunity, yet their global effects on human T cell states remain poorly defined. Here, we profile primary human T cell responses to 364 endogenous and microbiota-derived metabolites using high-throughput digital RNA with perturbation of genes sequencing (DRUG-seq), revealing structured transcriptional trajectories spanning baseline, metabolically primed, and highly activated states. We develop DRUG-seq-PerturbFormer, a multi-task deep learning framework that quantitatively captures perturbation magnitude and directionality across these states.

title: Niche-specific immune and microbial signatures across the healthy upper respiratory tract mucosa
creator: Nafsika Kardomatea, Jolanda Kool, Mioara A Nicolaie, Harry van Dijken, Emilie Reinen, Prokopis Konstanti, Dirk Eggink, Ryanne Jaarsma, Liesbeth van Emst, Esther van Woudenbergh, José A Ferreira, Susana Fuentes, Marien I de Jonge, Jørgen de Jonge, Lilly M Verhagen, Gerco den Hartog
description: SummaryHost-microbe interactions in the upper respiratory tract (URT) niches that form the first line of defense against respiratory infections are incompletely understood. We profiled immune and microbial features using minimally invasive samples from 44 healthy adults (20–65 years), including nasopharyngeal (NPS), oropharyngeal (OPS), and mid-turbinate nasal swabs (MTSs), mucosal lining fluid (MLF), and saliva.

title: Squamous cell carcinoma arising from ovarian mature cystic teratoma with concurrent cervical high-risk HPV infection and low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion: a case report
creator: Wenna Zhao, Yaxuan Sun, Masmuha Marshed Al Ramadhany, Ruochen Wu, Yifang Zhang
description: ObjectiveMalignant transformation of ovarian mature cystic teratoma (MCT) is uncommon, with squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) being the predominant type. Its pathogenesis remains poorly understood, and the potential role of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is controversial.Case reportA 58-year-old postmenopausal woman presented with a huge complex cystic-solid pelvic mass. The elevated Serum SCC antigen revealed potential malignant transformation.

title: Brain-binding auto-antibodies in subjects with and without post-COVID-syndrome after SARS-CoV-2 infection
creator: Majd Faraj, Karin Weissenborn, Bianca Teegen, Meike Dirks, Ann-Katrin Hennemann, Vanessa Wuttke, Winfried Stöcker, Nina Gödecke, Rainer Blasczyk, Anika Großhennig, Hannelore Ehrenreich, Gernot Beutel
description: Various pathomechanisms are discussed as possible causes of Post-COVID syndrome (PCS). Immune system dysfunction with increase of autoimmune responses is one of them. Whether the observed increase of autoantibody prevalence after COVID-19 is of any significance for the well-being of affected subjects in the long-term is controversial.

title: circHIPK3 promotes pro-fibrotic epithelial reprogramming via the miR-29a-3p/SPARC axis with associated enhancement of TGF-β/SMAD signaling
creator: Ying Zhou, Yixin Huang, Jiangpo Ma, Wei Wang, Zhongkai Tong, Yong Zhou, Yu Cao, Zhaoxing Dong
description: BackgroundIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is fatal with limited treatments. circHIPK3 is upregulated in fibrotic lungs, but its role in lung epithelial cells and connection to TGF-β/SMAD signaling are unclear.MethodsWe used TGF-β1-stimulated lung epithelial cells (A549, BEAS-2B) and a bleomycin-induced mouse model. circHIPK3 was silenced with ASOs.

title: Vezdaea minima, a new species of microlichen from Japan
creator: Takato Moriyama, Chihiro Tanaka
description: The genus Vezdaea consists of lichenized or alga-associated fungi and is characterized by small apothecia without exciple. Unidentified Vezdaea was collected in Japan and morphological observation was performed. The collected samples differed from any known species of the genus Vezdaea in the combination of net-like morphology of paraphyses and the size of the asci and ascospores.

title: Lipid profile alterations in pulmonary tuberculosis patients with and without diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Samuel Yahaya, Ibrahim Anyass Goumboundi, Roland Osei Saahene, Kwabena Dankwa, Samuel Acquah, Richard K. D. Ephraim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThis systematic review and meta-analysis explored lipid alterations associated with tuberculosis-diabetes comorbidity. We quantitatively synthesised the lipid parameters, comparing high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, and total cholesterol among patients with TB-DM comorbidity, TB-only, and DM-only.MethodsFollowing PRISMA guidelines and a registered protocol (PROSPERO: CRD420261355915), we searched PubMed (n = 150), Scopus (n = 679), and Google Scholar (n = 70) through April 7, 2026. Observational studies reporting lipid parameters were included.

title: Species groups and identification key to Chinese Temnothorax ants (Hymenoptera, Formicidae) with descriptions of four new species from Shennongjia National Park
creator: Fangchao Deng, Jingyuan Yang, Zhenghui Xu
description: The myrmicine ant genus Temnothorax Mayr, 1861 is highly diverse in China; however, its fauna remained inadequately studied until recently. During the 2023 Background Resources Survey Project in Shennongjia National Park, four new species of this genus were discovered and are herein described as Temnothorax shennongisp. nov., T. hubeiensissp. nov., T. zhaojunaesp. nov., and T. wangweiisp. nov.

title: Adopting information and communications technology in the control, prevention, and management of stroke: perspectives from patients and providers in Uganda
creator: Prossy Kiddu Namyalo, Robert Setekera, Primrose Nakazibwe
description: ObjectiveThe stroke burden in Uganda ranks ninth among the ten causes of death, a major cause of chronic illnesses, accounting for the top ten causes of hospitalization. This baseline study examined how mobile phones can improve the prevention, management, and treatment of stroke in rural Uganda.MethodsIt was a cross-sectional study that utilized a mixture of methods.

title: From images to health insight: integrating MLLM, NLP, and objective Q-sorting of nursing-home built environment orientations
creator: Si-Jie Li, Zi-Jie Zou, Xi Ye, Chunhua Lin
description: BackgroundPopulation aging has intensified pressure on global healthcare and social security systems, driving a shift in care from treatment-oriented approaches toward functional maintenance and chronic disease rehabilitation. How to design and optimize the built environment of nursing homes to support the physical and mental health of older adults has become an important issue in health policy and architectural design.

title: Hepatitis B virus infections in pregnant women and children in the era of HBV elimination
creator: Malgorzata Pawlowska
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In the hepatitis B virus (HBV) elimination strategy announced by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 2016, one of the main aspects is the prevention of vertical infections. In the prevention of vertical HBV infections, chemoprophylaxis with tenofovir is recommended from the 28th week of pregnancy in women with a high viral load (HBV DNA > 2 × 105 IU/ml) or the presence of HBeAg in the serum and active-passive immunoprophylaxis (HepB-BD+ HBIG) in all newborns born to mothers infected with HBV.

title: High-frequency ultrasound characterization of vulvar skin in patients with lichenoid vulvar dermatoses and correlation of its vascular index with microvessel density and microvessel area
creator: Jiyun Chen, Kaikai Shen, Jun Xv, Yujie Shi, Qiuyu Liu, Haohui Zhu, Xijun Zhang
description: ObjectivesWe utilized high-frequency ultrasound to characterize vulvar skin alterations in lichenoid vulvar dermatoses (LVD) and to determine whether the sonographic vascular index (VI) correlates with histopathological microvessel density (MVD) and microvessel area (MVA).MethodsThis study included thirty-seven patients with pathologically confirmed LVD who attended Henan Provincial People’s Hospital between December 2021 and May 2024.

title: Holdfast-Derived Lipid Extract from the Patagonian Macroalga Macrocystis pyrifera Attenuates Amyloid-β-Induced Neuronal Metabolic Dysfunction In Vitro and Ex Vivo
creator: Fabio Méndez, Pedro Cisternas, Paulina Ormazabal, Camila Gherardelli, Máximo Frangopulos, Andrés Mansilla, Nibaldo C. Inestrosa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Impaired cerebral glucose metabolism is an early and clinically relevant feature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Amyloid-β (Aβ) accumulation can further disrupt neuronal energy homeostasis, increasing metabolic and oxidative vulnerability. Objective: This study evaluated whether lipid extracts obtained from different morphological structures of the Patagonian macroalga could preserve neuronal glucose metabolism and viability under basal conditions and following exposure to an Aβ1–42 preparation generated under established oligomer-forming conditions.

title: Valvular thrombosis complicating tricuspid valve replacement: a case report
creator: Nugraha Teguh Palin, Achmad Lefi
description: Valvular heart disease is cardiovascular pathology that affects over 100 million people worldwide and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Although tricuspid valve disease is the least common primary valve pathology, it is linked to a significantly increased mortality rate (up to 42% within 3 years).

title: Effects of Printing Layer Thickness and Thermocycling on the Mechanical, Morphological, Optical, and Dimensional Properties of Directly Printed Clear Aligners
creator: Isra Dilshad Rostum, Omar Sabah Mohammed Jamil Ali
description: Directly printed clear aligners may streamline orthodontic workflows but must withstand intraoral aging. This in vitro study evaluated the effects of layer thickness (50, 100, and 150 µm) and thermocycling on mechanical, morphological, optical, and dimensional properties of Graphy Tera Harz TA-28 material.

title: Oral behaviors in Chinese temporomandibular disorder patients: insights from exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses
creator: Tiqian Liu, Adrian Ujin Yap, Yanyu Sun, Yunhao Zheng, Tianqi Wang, Shiya Zeng, Zhen Liu, Xin Xiong
description: AimThis study aimed to evaluate the factor structure of the Oral Behaviors Checklist (OBC) in Chinese temporomandibular disorder (TMDs) patients and compare the outcomes with those of Western patients. Additionally, it examined the correlations between different OBC subscale scoring methods.MethodsA total of 869 patients completed a survey that included demographic information, the Symptom Questionnaire, and OBC.

title: Assessing the Potential of Multispectral UAV-Derived Vegetation Indices for Estimating Water Use of Taro (Colocasia esculenta) Under Different Weed Management Practices
creator: Knowledge Muchaonyerwa, Maqsooda Mahomed, Shaeden Gokool, Alistair Clulow, Gary Denton, Kyle Reddy, Richard Kunz
description: Water availability is typically a limiting factor in rainfed sub-Saharan farming systems. Smallholder farmers in this region grow neglected and underutilized crops (NUCs) such as taro to supplement food shortages. Understanding the water use of NUCs could contribute to improving productivity. Traditional methods of monitoring actual evapotranspiration (ETa) are point-based and do not capture the variability in smallholder fields.

title: Early Radiographic Warning Signs of Impending Lemierre's Syndrome
creator: Richa S Nathan, Tyler J Ostrowski, Ananth Narayan, Neil Gildener-Leapman
description: Lemierre’s syndrome is a rare and potentially life-threatening complication of head and neck infections, such as bacterial pharyngitis or tonsillitis. It is characterized by the extension of infection into the lateral pharyngeal spaces, leading to subsequent septic thrombophlebitis of the internal jugular vein(s).

title: Rapid and visual detection of Tacheng tick virus 1 using loop-mediated isothermal amplification technique
creator: Qiqi Guo, Zheng Gui, Yuanning Ren, Ziyan Liu, Ning Liu, Liang Li, Zedong Wang, Jingfeng Yu
description: IntroductionTacheng tick virus 1 (TcTV-1) is an emerging tick-borne nairovirus associated with human febrile illness. To date, no reliable detection method for TcTV-1 has been established. In this study, we developed and evaluated a rapid loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) assay for the detection of TcTV-1.MethodsThe primers were designed based on the nucleocapsid protein (NP) gene of TcTV-1.

title: A Case Report of Spontaneous Pneumomediastinum (Hamman's Syndrome) During Labor
creator: Christopher Barrera-Hoffmann, Yadira Mariaca-Ortíz, Mauro Alejandro Rodríguez-Flota, Paul Alejandro Cerda-García, Enrique Monares-Zepeda
description: Hamman's syndrome is characterized by spontaneous pneumomediastinum triggered by Valsalva maneuvers and is an uncommon complication during labor and the postpartum period. It is typically benign and managed conservatively with oxygen therapy and analgesia. We present the clinical case of a 21-year-old primigravida who developed spontaneous pneumomediastinum during labor, manifesting with subcutaneous emphysema and dyspnea.

title: Determinants of abnormal liver-related biomarkers in adult COVID-19 patients
creator: Sijia Zhang, Yue Hu, Li Liu, Xianying Ning, Qiang Li, Guangqin Xiao
description: BackgroundSerum hepatic injury markers indexes are altered in COVID-19 patients. We aimed to explore the factors that could be associated with abnormal serum hepatic injury markers in adult COVID-19 patients.MethodsEight main hepatic injury markers were examined. Demographic and hematological information, mean CT values (MCTVs) of liver and pancreas, and abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness were recorded.

title: Combined Antegrade–Retrograde Cardioplegia for Myocardial Protection During Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting in Patients with Left Main Coronary Artery Disease: The CARDIOPROTECT-LMCAD Randomised Trial
creator: Jelena Lesanovic, Milan Milojevic, Djordje Nikolic, Ivan Soldatovic, Dragana Unic-Stojanovic, Igor Zivkovic, Miroslav Milicic, Petar Vukovic, Ivana Petrovic, Sinisa Jagodic, Milovan Bojic, Slobodan Micovic
description: Background and Objectives: Myocardial protection during on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) limits ischaemic injury, particularly in patients with left main coronary artery disease (LMCAD), in whom severe proximal stenosis may compromise antegrade cardioplegia delivery. We investigated whether combined antegrade–retrograde blood cardioplegia reduces postoperative high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) concentrations, a marker of perioperative myocardial injury.

title: Establishing serum protein electrophoresis reference intervals in free-ranging barren-ground caribou (Rangifer tarandus granti)
creator: Maris J. Daleo, Camilla Lieske, Carolyn Cray, Kimberlee B. Beckmen
description: Barren-ground caribou (Rangifer tarandus granti) populations range in parts of Alaska, USA, and the Yukon Territory, Canada, and are culturally and nutritionally important to northern Indigenous communities and subsistence hunters. Baseline clinical metrics in free-ranging caribou can inform individual and population health, signal environmental change, and guide conservation efforts.

title: Lung-resident lymphocytes and their roles in respiratory infections and chronic respiratory diseases
creator: Arka Sen Chaudhuri, Jie Sun
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recent scientific breakthroughs have blurred traditional boundaries between innate and adaptive immunity, revealing a sophisticated network of tissue-resident cells that deliver immediate, localized immune responses. These lymphocytes not only provide rapid frontline defense but also present a paradoxical role in the pathogenesis of respiratory diseases such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, pulmonary fibrosis, and the long-term tissue consequences of viral infections including severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2).

title: Impact of Female Reproductive Hormones on Surgically Induced Hemorrhage: A Translational Animal Model
creator: Nima Mehrjoh, Lucía De Miguel Gómez, Gennaro Selvaggi, Claes Ohlsson, Mats Hellström, Lars Rasmusson
description: Objectives: To establish an animal model for investigating the impact of female reproductive hormones on perioperative blood loss during cranio-maxillofacial surgery. Methods: Forty female Sprague-Dawley rats were sequentially allocated into five groups (n = 8 each): one sham-operated group (SHAM) receiving vehicle and four ovariectomized groups (OVX) receiving either the vehicle, 17β-estradiol, progesterone, or follicle-stimulating hormone-β.

title: Thoracic duct identification using three-dimensional thoracoscope versus indocyanine green fluorescence during minimally invasive esophagectomy: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Saiguang Ji, Fuchen Xing, Hai Zhou, Jian Xu, Chenyan Wang, Hong Liu
description: BackgroundChylothorax following esophagectomy is a frustrating complication with considerable morbidity. In addition, recognizing the morphological patterns of the thoracic duct (TD) holds great significance. This study was aimed at explore the safety and efficacy of three-dimensional (3D) thoracoscope in comparison with indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence to identify TD during minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) for esophageal cancer.

title: An observational study of the reliability and concurrent validity of heart rate variability devices in athletes
creator: Hedvig Johansson, Emily Adderley, Seán Clarke, Patrick McIntyre, Garreth Reilly, Brian Caulfield, Sinead Holden
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHeart rate variability (HRV) is a non-invasive indicator of autonomic nervous system function and is increasingly used in athlete monitoring. While electrocardiography (ECG) is the gold standard for HRV measurement, its use is limited in field settings.ObjectiveTo evaluate the intra-session reliability and concurrent validity of a smartphone-based PPG app for HRV measurement in athletes, compared to a Polar H10 chest strap and ECG.MethodsThis observational study included 37 trained participants (17 female; mean age 21.95 ± 3.69 years).

title: Optimizing Surgical Correction of Symblepharon Secondary to Lower Eyelid Burn Scar
creator: Andre Pinto, Manuel Caneira, Francisco Caneira, Diogo Conduto, Catarina Gouveia
description: The healing of lower eyelid injuries can lead to anatomical distortion and compromise the function of multiple periocular structures. To restore eyelid function and aesthetics, it is crucial to establish an accurate diagnosis and provide appropriate treatment to the affected structures.

title: Pasteurella multocida Bacteremia in an Immunocompromised Patient With Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report
creator: Rafaela Lopes Freitas, Fábio Reis, Eduarda Ruiz Pena
description: Pasteurella multocida (P. multocida) is a facultative anaerobic Gram-negative coccobacillus that represents a rare cause of systemic infection in immunocompromised patients.This report presents the case of a 59-year-old man with advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the oesophagus, recently undergoing radiotherapy and chemotherapy, halted due to cytopenias, including neutropenia.

title: Improving self-care, HbA1c control, and quality of life in type 2 diabetes: a self-regulation intervention based on the individual and family self-management theory
creator: Fadli Fadli, Nursalam Nursalam, Elly Lilianty Sjattar, Nilawati Uly
description: BackgroundType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains a global health challenge, often associated with poor self-care, inadequate glycemic control, and reduced quality of life. Conventional diabetes education mainly focuses on biomedical aspects, with limited attention to psychological self-regulation and family support, resulting in suboptimal outcomes.

title: Aspergillus Species as a Rare Cause of Primary Mycotic Aneurysm With Aortoenteric Fistula
creator: Fahad Alshubaily, Jumana A Fatani, Abdullah Almufarrih, Isam Osman
description: Aortoenteric fistula (AEF) is an abnormal connection between the aorta and the adjacent gastrointestinal (GI) tract and is often misdiagnosed in clinical practice. We present the case of a 65-year-old male, who presented with upper GI bleeding and melena. The patient underwent upper and lower GI examinations with no conclusive findings.

title: Pre-Impregnated Powder Coatings with a Thermoplastic Matrix for Use in Fibre-Reinforced Polymer Sandwich Composites: Manufacturing, Mechanical Testing and Finite Element Modelling
creator: Przemysław Golewski, Michał Budka
description: This study presents a manufacturing route for pre-impregnated functional powder coatings (PCs) intended for fibre-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites, including vacuum-infused sandwich structures. PCs comprising powder, thermoplastic nonwoven and twill glass fabric were produced by a two-stage heat-pressing process. Ceramic, mineral and metallic powders were investigated.

title: Effect of Denture Base Stiffness on Stress Redistribution in an Idealized Complete-Denture Model Under Static Bilateral Clenching: A Finite Element Analysis
creator: Jeong-Hee Seo, Jeong-Hyeon Lee, Won-Gi Kim, Sung-Jae Lee, Bongju Kim, Dong-Wook Han
description: Denture base elastic-property assignment may influence how mechanical stress is distributed between a complete denture and its supporting tissues. This study compared rigid and flexible denture base material conditions in an idealized maxillomandibular finite element (FE) model at the final static bilateral clenching step. The model represented a fully edentulous geometry with coincident denture–gingiva surfaces connected by a tie constraint.

title: Correction: Association between trait mindfulness and self-efficacy in sports-disadvantaged college students in China: the chain mediating role of exercise motivation and persistence
creator: Kuo Xu, Lin Zhu, Yun Li, Yang Cao, Guodong Zhang
description: SE 95% Bootstrapping CI p-value Direct effect0.1950.0360.125–0.266<0.001Total indirect0.3960.0300.340–0.455<0.001Indirect effect 10.2240.0260.176–0.277<0.001Indirect effect 20.1000.0180.067–0.136<0.001Indirect effect 30.0720.0130.050–0.0990.002Total effect0.5910.0340.525–0.658<0.001SE, standard error; Indirect effect 1 = trait mindfulness → Exercise motivation → self-efficacy; Indirect effect 2 = Trait mindfulness → Exercise persistence → self-efficacy; Indirect effect 3 = Trait Mindfulness → Exercise motivation → exercise persistence → Self-efficacy. Significance levels: ***p < 0.
